literature.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 所有分析的分离株均属于东北亚谱系,主要在 2016 年至 2017 年左右分为两个区域分支(tMRCA:HA,2017 年 12 月;NA,2016 年 11 月)。尽管蒙古和韩国之间地理距离遥远,但这些 H6N1 分离株在东北亚谱系内表现出密切的遗传连通性(贝叶斯因子 > 100)。 [10.1007/s00705-026-06705-2]
在距离农场 2 公里范围内采样的 12 只猫中,有 3 只具有针对 H5N1 病毒的中和抗体,并且靠近奶牛场是血清阳性的一个具有统计学意义的风险因素。 [10.3201/eid3209.260785]
该研究确定新南威尔士州 (NSW) 和维多利亚州 (VIC) 的 HPAI H5N1 家禽 暴发 预测风险最高,西澳大利亚州 (WA)、南澳大利亚州 (SA) 和塔斯马尼亚州 (TAS) 也有其他高风险地区。相比之下,北领地 (NT) 和昆士兰 (QLD) 的大部分地区、西澳和南澳预计风险较低。 [10.64898/2026.07.27.740638]
新兴的 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b 病毒(但不是历史的 H5 谱系)结合人 MHC-II HLA-DR 并介导不依赖唾液酸的细胞进入;结合随 MHC-II 表达和 HLA-DR 等位基因变异而变化;来自 clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive 人类的交叉反应单克隆抗体可以阻断这种相互作用。 [10.64898/2026.07.22.739677]
NI-ELLA 与用于抗体检测的商业 ELISA 具有很强的相关性,并且终点滴度与病毒中和滴度具有良好的相关性。无论 PCR 结果如何,与病毒分离阳性样品相比,散装罐牛奶样品在病毒分离阴性样品中显示出更高的检出率和更强的抗体滴度。 [10.3389/fvets.2026.1902594]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: All analyzed isolates belonged to the Northeast Asian lineage, primarily diverging into two regional subclades around 2016–2017 (tMRCA: HA, Dec 2017; NA, Nov 2016). [10.1007/s00705-026-06705-2]

Three of the 12 cats sampled within 2 km of farms had neutralizing antibodies against H5N1 virus, and proximity to dairy farms was a statistically significant risk factor for seropositivity. [10.3201/eid3209.260785]

The study identified New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) as having the highest predicted risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks, with additional high-risk areas in Western Australia (WA), South Australia (SA), and Tasmania (TAS). [10.64898/2026.07.27.740638]

Emerging H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not historical H5 lineages, bind human MHC-II HLA-DR and mediate sialic acid-independent cell entry; binding varies with MHC-II expression and HLA-DR allelic variation; and cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies from clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive humans can block this interaction. [10.64898/2026.07.22.739677]
NI-ELLA demonstrated strong correlation with commercial ELISAs for antibody detection, and endpoint titers correlated well with virus neutralization titers. [10.3389/fvets.2026.1902594]

brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
All analyzed isolates belonged to the Northeast Asian lineage, primarily diverging into two regional subclades around 2016–2017 (tMRCA: HA, Dec 2017; NA, Nov 2016). [10.1007/s00705-026-06705-2].

Three of the 12 cats sampled within 2 km of farms had neutralizing antibodies against H5N1 virus, and proximity to dairy farms was a statistically significant risk factor for seropositivity. [10.3201/eid3209.260785].

news.lead_en: Victoria, Australia, has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain, detected in a greater crested tern near Portland.
key_findings_en: Victoria confirmed its first H5N1 bird flu case in a greater crested tern near Portland.
Authorities are urging poultry keepers to house their birds for at least 14 days to reduce transmission risk.
The H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been declared ineradicable, with $113 million allocated for response efforts.
news.trend_or_risk_en: The spread of H5N1 avian influenza in Australia is increasing, posing a potential risk to wildlife and the poultry industry.
news.caveats_en: No large-scale mortality has been reported yet, and the virus has not spread to poultry.
news.brief_en: Victoria, Australia, has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain, detected in a greater crested tern near Portland. Testing confirmed the bird had contracted the virus, prompting authorities to increase surveillance of wild animal populations and urge poultry keepers to house their birds for at least 14 days. The H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been declared ineradicable, with the Australian government committing $113 million to response efforts. While the risk to human health is very low, authorities are concerned about potential impacts on poultry and wildlife, with previous outbreaks resulting in millions of birds being euthanized. Community cooperation is highlighted as crucial for controlling the spread.

papers.title: H5N1 influenza binding and cell entry via human class II MHC, and blocking by cross-reactive antibodies
papers.abstract: Summary paragraph Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses are currently responsible for a multi-species outbreak affecting wild birds, poultry, numerous mammalian species, and humans. Influenza A viruses typically initiate infection through binding to sialic acid, although select bat and human influenza viruses can also exploit class II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II) molecules for cell entry. Here we show that emerging H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not historical H5 lineages, bind human MHC-II HLA-DR and mediate sialic acid-independent cell entry. Hemagglutinin binding to primary human immune cells varies with MHC-II expression and is further shaped by HLA-DR allelic variation, identifying host genetic determinants that may influence susceptibility to infection. Mammalian-adaptive substitutions within the hemagglutinin sialic acid receptor-binding domain reduce MHC-II binding, suggesting this interaction is remodeled during clade 2.3.4.4b H5 adaptation to a human host. Lastly, cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies isolated from clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive humans can block the hemagglutinin–MHC-II interaction. These findings identify a previously unrecognized receptor pathway in contemporary H5N1 viruses and reveal that both human genetic variation and pre-existing humoral immunity can modulate this interaction, with implications for host range, cellular tropism, spillover risk, and therapeutic intervention.

papers.title_zh: H5N1 流感通过人 II 类 MHC 结合和进入细胞,并通过交叉反应抗体阻断
papers.source_body_en: Summary paragraph Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses are currently responsible for a multi-species outbreak affecting wild birds, poultry, numerous mammalian species, and humans. Influenza A viruses typically initiate infection through binding to sialic acid, although select bat and human influenza viruses can also exploit class II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II) molecules for cell entry. Here we show that emerging H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not historical H5 lineages, bind human MHC-II HLA-DR and mediate sialic acid-independent cell entry. Hemagglutinin binding to primary human immune cells varies with MHC-II expression and is further shaped by HLA-DR allelic variation, identifying host genetic determinants that may influence susceptibility to infection. Mammalian-adaptive substitutions within the hemagglutinin sialic acid receptor-binding domain reduce MHC-II binding, suggesting this interaction is remodeled during clade 2.3.4.4b H5 adaptation to a human host. Lastly, cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies isolated from clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive humans can block the hemagglutinin–MHC-II interaction. These findings identify a previously unrecognized receptor pathway in contemporary H5N1 viruses and reveal that both human genetic variation and pre-existing humoral immunity can modulate this interaction, with implications for host range, cellular tropism, spillover risk, and therapeutic intervention.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要段落 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 病毒目前负责影响 野生鸟类、家禽、众多哺乳动物物种和人类的多物种 暴发。甲型流感病毒通常通过与唾液酸结合来启动感染,尽管某些蝙蝠和人类流感病毒也可以利用 II 类主要组织相容性复合物 (MHC-II) 分子进入细胞。在这里,我们表明新兴的 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b 病毒(而不是历史的 H5 谱系)结合人类 MHC-II HLA-DR 并介导不依赖唾液酸的细胞进入。血凝素与初级人类免疫细胞的结合随 MHC-II 表达的变化而变化,并进一步受到 HLA-DR 等位基因变异的影响,从而识别出可能影响感染易感性的 宿主 遗传决定因素。血凝素唾液酸受体结合域内的哺乳动物适应性取代减少了 MHC-II 结合,表明这种相互作用在进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5 适应人类 宿主 过程中被重塑。最后,从 clade 2.3.4.4b H5-naive 人类中分离出的交叉反应单克隆抗体可以阻断血凝素 - MHC-II 相互作用。这些发现确定了当代 H5N1 病毒中以前未被识别的受体途径,并揭示人类遗传变异和预先存在的体液免疫可以调节这种相互作用,对 宿主 范围、细胞向性、跨物种溢出 风险和治疗干预具有影响。

papers.title: HPAI H5N1 risk in Australia: a model for the prediction of poultry outbreaks
papers.abstract: The panzootic highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus has now been detected on the Australian mainland, with incursions from the sub-Antarctic region posing an increasing threat to domestic wildlife and poultry populations. Our study aimed to predict the risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks across Australia at the local government area (LGA) level using a range of influential risk factors. We first used a Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model to estimate the environmental suitability for HPAI H5N1 occurrence across Australia. The resulting suitability layer was then integrated with five additional predictor layers, including abundance data for two Southern Ocean wild birds, one of which has introduced HPAI H5N1 into Australia; abundance data for 28 native Australian wild birds; native bird flyways across Australia; Australian chicken density; and poultry farm density. The six layers were aggregated and averaged to generate an HPAI H5N1 risk map for poultry outbreaks across Australian LGAs. Although most incursions have occurred in Western Australia (WA) and South Australia (SA), we identified New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) as having the highest predicted risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks. Additional high-risk areas were identified in WA, SA, and Tasmania (TAS). In contrast, the Northern Territory (NT) and large parts of Queensland (QLD), WA, and SA were predicted to be at low risk. These findings provide a spatially explicit framework to support targeted surveillance, preparedness, and biosecurity measures aimed at mitigating the impact of future HPAI H5N1 outbreaks in Australian poultry.

Our study aimed to predict the risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks across Australia at the local government area (LGA) level using a range of influential risk factors. We first used a Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model to estimate the environmental suitability for HPAI H5N1 occurrence across Australia. The resulting suitability layer was then integrated with five additional predictor layers, including abundance data for two Southern Ocean wild birds, one of which has introduced HPAI H5N1 into Australia; abundance data for 28 native Australian wild birds; native bird flyways across Australia; Australian chicken density; and poultry farm density. The six layers were aggregated and averaged to generate an HPAI H5N1 risk map for poultry outbreaks across Australian LGAs. Although most incursions have occurred in Western Australia (WA) and South Australia (SA), we identified New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) as having the highest predicted risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks. Additional high-risk areas were identified in WA, SA, and Tasmania (TAS). In contrast, the Northern Territory (NT) and large parts of Queensland (QLD), WA, and SA were predicted to be at low risk. These findings provide a spatially explicit framework to support targeted surveillance, preparedness, and biosecurity measures aimed at mitigating the impact of future HPAI H5N1 outbreaks in Australian poultry.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing threat of HPAI H5N1 to Australian poultry and wildlife, particularly from sub-Antarctic incursions, by predicting outbreak risks at the local government area (LGA) level.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a MaxEnt model to estimate environmental suitability for HPAI H5N1 occurrence across Australia, integrating data on bird abundance, flyways, and poultry density to generate a risk map for LGAs.
analysis.methods: A Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model was employed to estimate environmental suitability for HPAI H5N1, and this was combined with five additional predictor layers, including wild bird abundance, bird flyways, and poultry density data.
analysis.main_results: The study identified New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) as having the highest predicted risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks, with additional high-risk areas in Western Australia (WA), South Australia (SA), and Tasmania (TAS). In contrast, the Northern Territory (NT) and large parts of Queensland (QLD), WA, and SA were predicted to be at low risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as a spatially explicit framework for targeted surveillance and biosecurity measures, offering a novel approach to predict HPAI H5N1 risk in Australian poultry.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance, preparedness, and biosecurity strategies to mitigate the impact of future HPAI H5N1 outbreaks in Australian poultry.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on predictive modeling and does not include empirical validation of outbreak predictions, which may limit the confidence in its results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of modeled data rather than direct observation.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the risk of HPAI H5N1 outbreaks in Australian poultry by developing a predictive model that integrates environmental and biological factors. The research highlights the increasing threat of sub-Antarctic incursions and identifies high-risk areas such as New South Wales and Victoria, while noting lower risk in regions like the Northern Territory. The model provides a spatially explicit framework for targeted surveillance and biosecurity measures. However, the study's reliance on predictive modeling without empirical validation limits the confidence in its results, indicating moderate evidence strength. The findings have significant implications for public health and avian influenza management in Australia.

papers.title: Immunization with deglycosylated H7N9 VLP enhances cross-strain protective antibody responses against avian influenza H7N9 variants in mice
papers.abstract: Introduction The rapidly evolving avian influenza H7N9 virus remains a threaten to public health globally. There is an urgent need to develop broad-spectrum vaccines capable of eliciting functional cross-strain protective immunity against emerging viral variants. Methods N-linked glycosylation can shield critical residues from immune recognition. Here, a prototype virus-like particle (VLP) was constructed based on the antigenic sequences derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus. Glycosidase enzymes were utilized to trim the glycan molecules for generating monoglycosylated VLP (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) derivates. The structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity of these VLPs were systematically evaluated. Results Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity like the fully glycosylated prototype VLP (VLPfg). Immunization with deglycosylated VLPs induced robust virus-specific antibodies and a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile in mice, whereas the titers were comparable to that of VLPfg. Among them, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 virus strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactive antibody responses. Conclusion This study demonstrated the enzymatic deglycosylation of influenza H7N9 VLP improves the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice. The nonglycosylated H7N9 VLP represents a potential vaccine candidate to against the threat of antigenically divergent H7N9 virus variants.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza H7N9 poses an ongoing public health threat, and existing vaccines may not provide sufficient cross-strain protection against antigenically divergent variants. The study addresses the need for broad-spectrum vaccines that can elicit functional cross-strain immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study constructed virus-like particles (VLPs) based on the antigenic sequences of the A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus and evaluated their structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity in mice.
analysis.methods: N-linked glycosylation was enzymatically trimmed to generate monoglycosylated (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated (VLPng) VLPs, which were then assessed for hemagglutination activity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity.
analysis.main_results: Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity comparable to the fully glycosylated prototype VLP. Immunization with VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 strains than VLPmg or VLPfg.

papers.title_zh: 去糖基化 H7N9 VLP 免疫可增强小鼠针对 禽流感 H7N9 变种的跨品系保护性抗体反应
papers.source_body_en: Introduction The rapidly evolving avian influenza H7N9 virus remains a threaten to public health globally. There is an urgent need to develop broad-spectrum vaccines capable of eliciting functional cross-strain protective immunity against emerging viral variants. Methods N-linked glycosylation can shield critical residues from immune recognition. Here, a prototype virus-like particle (VLP) was constructed based on the antigenic sequences derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus. Glycosidase enzymes were utilized to trim the glycan molecules for generating monoglycosylated VLP (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) derivates. The structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity of these VLPs were systematically evaluated. Results Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity like the fully glycosylated prototype VLP (VLPfg). Immunization with deglycosylated VLPs induced robust virus-specific antibodies and a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile in mice, whereas the titers were comparable to that of VLPfg. Among them, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 virus strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactive antibody responses. Conclusion This study demonstrated the enzymatic deglycosylation of influenza H7N9 VLP improves the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice. The nonglycosylated H7N9 VLP represents a potential vaccine candidate to against the threat of antigenically divergent H7N9 virus variants.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介 快速进化的 禽流感 H7N9 病毒仍然对全球公共卫生构成威胁。迫切需要开发广谱 疫苗,能够引发针对新出现的病毒变种的功能性跨毒株保护性免疫。方法 N-连接糖基化可以保护关键残基免受免疫识别。在这里,基于 A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 病毒的抗原序列构建了原型病毒样颗粒 (VLP)。利用糖苷酶修剪聚糖分子,以生成单糖基化 VLP (VLPmg) 和非糖基化 VLP (VLPng) 衍生物。对这些 VLP 的结构完整性、抗原性和免疫原性进行了系统评估。结果 VLPmg 和 VLPng 均保持与完全糖基化原型 VLP (VLPfg) 一样的血凝活性和抗原性。用去糖基化的 VLP 进行免疫可以在小鼠体内诱导出强大的病毒特异性抗体和平衡的 Th1/Th2 免疫特征,而滴度与 VLPfg 相当。其中,VLPng针对不同的H7N9病毒株诱导了更高的血凝抑制和中和抗体滴度,表明跨病毒株反应性抗体反应得到改善。结论 这项研究表明,流感 H7N9 VLP 的酶促去糖基化可改善小鼠体内广泛保护性抗体反应的诱导。非糖基化的 H7N9 VLP 代表了潜在的 疫苗 候选药物,可对抗抗原不同的 H7N9 病毒变种的威胁。

papers.title: Beyond H5N1: influenza A virus infection in bovine udder organoids.
papers.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) have recently expanded their host range to bovine species, raising critical questions about tissue tropism, viral replication capacity, and impacts on dairy production and zoonotic risk. Extensive shedding of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) H5N1 in milk from naturally infected cattle in the USA highlights the bovine mammary gland as a relevant site of viral replication. To investigate these dynamics, we established and characterized bovine mammary gland organoids (MGOs) derived from primary epithelial cells and maintained in chemically defined media. This efficient, scalable model reconstructs structural and functional hallmarks of the bovine udder, including luminal-basal polarity, lineage-specific cytokeratin patterns, and lactation-associated differentiation. We then used this system to study low and highly pathogenic avian, as well as swine and human IAVs. Viruses from diverse host species productively infected MGOs, largely independent of culturing conditions. Mammalian origin H1N1 strains matched bovine H5N1 in efficiency, but low pathogenic avian H9N2 showed restricted replication, indicating subtype-specific differences in mammary tropism. This suitability study develops a MGO platform that provides a tractable basis for detailed molecular investigation of mammary infection biology and influenza pathogenesis in cattle, to inform strategies that protect both animal and public health.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Influenza A viruses have recently expanded their host range to bovine species, raising critical questions about tissue tropism, viral replication capacity, and impacts on dairy production and zoonotic risk.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: To investigate these dynamics, we established and characterized bovine mammary gland organoids (MGOs) derived from primary epithelial cells and maintained in chemically defined media.

papers.title_zh: H5N1 之外:牛乳房类器官中的甲型流感病毒感染。
papers.source_body_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) have recently expanded their host range to bovine species, raising critical questions about tissue tropism, viral replication capacity, and impacts on dairy production and zoonotic risk. Extensive shedding of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) H5N1 in milk from naturally infected cattle in the USA highlights the bovine mammary gland as a relevant site of viral replication. To investigate these dynamics, we established and characterized bovine mammary gland organoids (MGOs) derived from primary epithelial cells and maintained in chemically defined media. This efficient, scalable model reconstructs structural and functional hallmarks of the bovine udder, including luminal-basal polarity, lineage-specific cytokeratin patterns, and lactation-associated differentiation. We then used this system to study low and highly pathogenic avian, as well as swine and human IAVs. Viruses from diverse host species productively infected MGOs, largely independent of culturing conditions. Mammalian origin H1N1 strains matched bovine H5N1 in efficiency, but low pathogenic avian H9N2 showed restricted replication, indicating subtype-specific differences in mammary tropism. This suitability study develops a MGO platform that provides a tractable basis for detailed molecular investigation of mammary infection biology and influenza pathogenesis in cattle, to inform strategies that protect both animal and public health.

papers.title: Mutations in severe human H5N1 cases facilitate evasion from human mucus and antivirals
papers.abstract: In late 2024, two individuals in Canada and the United States were treated in intensive care for acute respiratory distress caused by infection with the avian Influenza A Virus H5N1 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1. Viral sequence data obtained from sampling these patients indicated mixed alleles at haemagglutinin (HA) positions 190 and 226. Mutations at these positions are key determinants of HA usage of α2,6-linked sialic acids (SA), the most abundant influenza receptors in human upper respiratory tracts. Thus, these mutations raised concerns about human adaptation and pandemic potential of the H5N1 virus. In this study, we investigated the impact of the mutations at residues 190 and 226 in H5 HA. We studied the receptor binding properties, cell entry phenotypes and fitness impacts of the mutations using recombinant proteins, pseudotyped lentiviruses, and in the context of influenza viruses using reverse genetics. The mutations did not confer any detectable α2,6-linked sialic acid receptor usage either alone or in combination. Rather, viruses carrying these mutations exhibit weakened binding towards α2,3-linked sialic acid receptors. This correlated with an enhanced capacity to evade human airway mucus, and a reduced susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir. This research underscores that in addition to the way HA interacts with SA as entry receptors, other factors that impact the HA/NA balance might influence the evolutionary trajectory of a zoonotic virus in the human respiratory tract. This study presents a new paradigm for the evolutionary drivers of HA, where reduced sialic acid binding can serve as an advantage for escape from host barriers and antivirals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was motivated by the need to understand the potential for avian influenza A viruses to adapt to humans, as two individuals in Canada and the United States were treated in intensive care for acute respiratory distress caused by infection with the H5N1 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved analyzing viral sequence data from two patients infected with the H5N1 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1, who were treated in intensive care for acute respiratory distress. The research focused on the mutations at HA positions 190 and 226 observed in these cases.
analysis.methods: The researchers used recombinant proteins, pseudotyped lentiviruses, and reverse genetics to study the receptor binding properties, cell entry phenotypes, and fitness impacts of the mutations at HA residues 190 and 226 in the context of influenza viruses.
analysis.main_results: The mutations at HA positions 190 and 226 did not confer detectable α2,6-linked sialic acid receptor usage either alone or in combination. Instead, viruses with these mutations showed weakened binding towards α2,3-linked sialic acid receptors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that mutations in HA can lead to reduced sialic acid binding, which may provide an advantage for the virus to evade host barriers and antivirals, presenting a new paradigm for the evolutionary drivers of HA.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results have implications for understanding the adaptation of avian influenza viruses to humans and could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and the development of antiviral strategies against zoonotic influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on data from two patients, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong as it directly examines the receptor binding properties and fitness impacts of the mutations in the context of influenza viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of mutations at HA positions 190 and 226 in H5N1 avian influenza viruses, which were identified in two severe human cases in 2024. The researchers used recombinant proteins, pseudotyped lentiviruses, and reverse genetics to assess receptor binding, cell entry, and fitness. The results showed that these mutations did not enhance α2,6-linked sialic acid receptor usage but instead weakened binding to α2,3-linked sialic acids. This was associated with increased evasion of human airway mucus and reduced susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir. The study highlights that reduced sialic acid binding may provide an evolutionary advantage for avian influenza viruses to adapt to human hosts, offering new insights into the factors influencing their pathogenicity and potential for pandemic spread.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及分析两名感染 H5N1 2.3.4.4b 基因型 D1.1 的患者的病毒序列数据,这两名患者因急性呼吸窘迫而在重症监护室接受治疗。研究重点是在这些病例中观察到的 HA 位点 190 和 226 处的 突变。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用重组蛋白、假型慢病毒和反向遗传学来研究流感病毒中 突变 在 HA 残基 190 和 226 处的受体结合特性、细胞进入表型和适应性影响。
elements_zh.main_results: HA位置190和226处的突变不赋予可检测的α2,6-连接的唾液酸受体单独或组合使用。相反,带有这些 突变 的病毒与 α2,3 连接唾液酸受体的结合减弱。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,HA中的突变可导致唾液酸结合减少,这可能为病毒逃避宿主屏障和抗病毒药物提供优势,为HA的进化驱动因素提供了新的范例。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解 禽流感 病毒对人类的适应具有重要意义,并可为 监测、诊断 以及针对人畜共患流感的 抗病毒药物 策略的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于两名患者的数据,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它直接检查了 突变 在流感病毒背景下的受体结合特性和适应性影响。

papers.title: Evaluation of serologic assays for detection and quantification of influenza antibodies in milk samples from H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus infected dairy cows
papers.abstract: Since the confirmation of H5N1 HPAI virus in US dairy cattle on March 25, 2024, the bovine HPAI outbreak has continued with more than 1,000 confirmed herds in 19 states reported as of April 2, 2026. To ensure ongoing monitoring of HPAI spread, additional serologic assays have been evaluated to complement existing commercial ELISAs and molecular tools that underpin current epidemiological approaches. We previously established an N1 antibody-specific neuraminidase inhibition (NI)-enzyme linked lectin assay (ELLA) for DIVA (differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals) surveillance to detect H5N1 infection in vaccinated poultry with inactivated heterologous NA subtype (H5N9) vaccine. In this study, we applied NI-ELLA for the detection and quantification of N1 antibody in individual ( n = 110) and bulk tank ( n = 104) bovine milk samples. We demonstrated that both untreated samples and infranatant collected by centrifugation followed by heat inactivation can be used for different serologic assays depending on sample quality. There was a strong correlation in antibody detection between NI-ELLA and commercial ELISAs. Endpoint titers determined by NI-ELLA also correlated well with virus neutralization titers, which are used to evaluate protective antibody levels in milk samples. Detection and quantification of N1 antibodies in bulk tank milk samples further showed higher detection rates and stronger antibody titers among virus isolation-negative samples (regardless of the presence or absence of viral RNA detected by PCR) compared to virus isolation-positive samples. Higher levels of neutralizing antibody likely contributed to the lack of infectious virus detection depending on the stage of viral infection when milk was collected. Future studies are warranted to describe the duration and dynamics of antibody responses in milk samples over extended periods across individual cows, and NI-ELLA will serve as a valuable quantitative tool for evaluating antibody responses in those studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to evaluate additional serologic assays for monitoring the spread of H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in dairy cattle, complementing existing commercial ELISAs and molecular tools. The objective was to assess the N1 antibody-specific neuraminidase inhibition (NI)-enzyme linked lectin assay (ELLA) for detecting and quantifying antibodies in milk samples from infected cows.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study applied NI-ELLA to detect and quantify N1 antibodies in individual (n = 110) and bulk tank (n = 104) bovine milk samples collected from H5N1 HPAI virus-infected dairy cows. The samples were processed using untreated preparations and infranatant collected by centrifugation followed by heat inactivation.
analysis.methods: The researchers used an established N1 antibody-specific NI-ELLA for DIVA (differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals) surveillance. Antibody detection and quantification were performed on both individual and bulk tank milk samples, with comparisons made to commercial ELISAs and virus neutralization titers.
analysis.main_results: NI-ELLA demonstrated strong correlation with commercial ELISAs for antibody detection, and endpoint titers correlated well with virus neutralization titers. Bulk tank milk samples showed higher detection rates and stronger antibody titers in virus isolation-negative samples compared to virus isolation-positive samples, regardless of PCR results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that higher levels of neutralizing antibodies likely contributed to the lack of infectious virus detection, depending on the infection stage when milk was collected. The novelty lies in the validation of NI-ELLA as a quantitative tool for monitoring antibody responses in bovine milk samples.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support NI-ELLA as a valuable quantitative tool for surveillance and evaluating antibody dynamics in H5N1-infected dairy cattle, enhancing epidemiological monitoring and outbreak management. Future studies can leverage this method to describe antibody responses over extended periods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study focused on a specific assay and sample type without broader generalizability. Limitations include the reliance on a single geographic outbreak and the need for further validation across diverse populations and timeframes.

Applied to individual (n = 110) and bulk tank (n = 104) samples, NI-ELLA showed strong correlation with commercial ELISAs and virus neutralization titers. Bulk tank samples exhibited higher antibody titers in virus isolation-negative cases, suggesting neutralizing antibodies may limit virus detection. The assay serves as a quantitative tool for surveillance, with future studies needed to characterize antibody dynamics over time. The findings enhance epidemiological monitoring of H5N1 outbreaks in cattle.

papers.title_zh: H5N1 高致病性禽流感 病毒感染奶牛牛奶样品中流感抗体检测和定量血清学测定的评估
papers.source_body_en: Since the confirmation of H5N1 HPAI virus in US dairy cattle on March 25, 2024, the bovine HPAI outbreak has continued with more than 1,000 confirmed herds in 19 states reported as of April 2, 2026. To ensure ongoing monitoring of HPAI spread, additional serologic assays have been evaluated to complement existing commercial ELISAs and molecular tools that underpin current epidemiological approaches. We previously established an N1 antibody-specific neuraminidase inhibition (NI)-enzyme linked lectin assay (ELLA) for DIVA (differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals) surveillance to detect H5N1 infection in vaccinated poultry with inactivated heterologous NA subtype (H5N9) vaccine. In this study, we applied NI-ELLA for the detection and quantification of N1 antibody in individual ( n = 110) and bulk tank ( n = 104) bovine milk samples. We demonstrated that both untreated samples and infranatant collected by centrifugation followed by heat inactivation can be used for different serologic assays depending on sample quality. There was a strong correlation in antibody detection between NI-ELLA and commercial ELISAs. Endpoint titers determined by NI-ELLA also correlated well with virus neutralization titers, which are used to evaluate protective antibody levels in milk samples. Detection and quantification of N1 antibodies in bulk tank milk samples further showed higher detection rates and stronger antibody titers among virus isolation-negative samples (regardless of the presence or absence of viral RNA detected by PCR) compared to virus isolation-positive samples. Higher levels of neutralizing antibody likely contributed to the lack of infectious virus detection depending on the stage of viral infection when milk was collected. Future studies are warranted to describe the duration and dynamics of antibody responses in milk samples over extended periods across individual cows, and NI-ELLA will serve as a valuable quantitative tool for evaluating antibody responses in those studies.

Thursday, July 30, 2026 Australia: CSIRO Reports 4 H5 Positive Crested Tern Samples from Kangaroo Island Credit Wikipedia#19,270No sooner has I posted my last blog when the following statement was posted on the Australian government website:30 July 2026Attributable to Australian Chief Veterinary Officer, Dr Beth Cookson:Testing at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness (ACDP) has returned four positive results in crested terns, from Kangaroo Island, South Australia.There have now been 33 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu in Australia.All of these have been wild seabirds found in coastal locations.There remains no evidence of any mass mortality events and there are no detections in poultry or in our agricultural production system. The risk to human health remains low.While not particularly surprising given its proximity to the other SA confirmed seabirds, this is a concern because Kangaroo Island is home to a number of marine mammals which are known to be susceptible to avian flu, including:Australian sea lion.Australian fur seal.New Zealand fur seal.Bottlenose dolphin and common dolphin. Last October H5N1 was detected on Australia's Heard Island - which we recently revisited in Preprint: Mass mortality of southern elephant seals during multi-species outbreak of HPAI H5N1 on sub-Antarctic Heard Island - which reported:Drone surveys revealed mass mortality in southern elephant seals, with 8,573 pups (62%) recorded dead across Heard Island by the final surveys. Mortality increased at an average rate of 5.6% per day in a subset of harems, and the highest observed mortality in a harem was 97%. Based on the average (76%) mortality in the final surveys, total estimated pup mortality at Heard Island was 13,359 (from a total population of 17,364 pups), though this may be an underestimate as mortality was ongoing at this time. HPAI was detected in six of nine species tested and, we suspect, led to elevated mortality in king and gentoo penguins.While there is currently no evidence of spillover into Kangaroo Island's marine or terrestrial mammalian population, this is another worrisome milestone for HPAI as it spreads across Oceania. Australia: H5N1 Reaches Victoria - SA `Suspect' Count Rises (n=24) #19,269A few hours ago Victoria announced their first H5N1 detection, once again in a greater crested tern, this time found in Portland. We've two announcements, first from Agriculture Victoria, and second by Australian Chief Veterinary Officer, Dr Beth Cookson announcing the confirmation from CSIRO. H5N1 avian influenza strain detected in Victoria30 July 2026The high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 strain (H5 bird flu) has been detected in Victoria.Victoria’s Chief Veterinary Officer Dr Graeme Cooke said this detection is a result of Australia’s response to H5 bird flu, with the Victorian Government undertaking surveillance for the disease and working closely with the Commonwealth, interstate jurisdictions and industry partners.‘Preliminary testing has indicated H5 bird flu in a single greater crested tern found in Portland. Further genetic testing is underway at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness at Geelong to formally confirm this result.’ Dr Cooke said.‘This follows confirmation of the disease in seabirds in Western Australia, South Australia, New South Wales and Queensland, and the national decision that H5 bird flu is no longer technically feasible to eradicate in wildlife.’‘Following weeks of enhanced readiness, we have now enacted Victoria’s State Emergency Animal Disease Response Plan. Based on international experience, this H5 variant differs from previous strains and has been known to cause large numbers of deaths in wild birds and some mammals.’‘Our plans aim to limit impacts where possible particularly on our most threatened species, while also supporting our farmers and reducing risk to domestic and commercial poultry.‘We need Victorians to avoid contact with sick or dead wildlife, record what they see and report it. Early reporting gives us the best chance to reduce the impacts of the disease,’ Dr Cooke said. (Continue . . . ) 30 July 2026Attributable to Australian Chief Veterinary Officer, Dr Beth Cookson:Testing at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness (ACDP) has confirmed H5 bird flu in a greater crested tern, found in Portland in Victoria.This is the first case in the state of Victoria.There have now been 29 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu in Australia.All of these have been wild seabirds found in coastal locations.There remains no evidence of any mass mortality events and there are no detections in poultry or in our agricultural production system.The risk to human health remains lowMeanwhile, South Australia has confirmed a 15th case (a Giant Petrel), and reports an additional 24 suspect cases are pending confirmation by CSIRO.Current situationSouth Australia’s first confirmed detection of H5 bird flu was in a wild migratory bird (southern giant petrel) on Wednesday, 24 June at Knights Beach at Port Elliot on the Fleurieu Peninsula.Further confirmed detections include a giant petrel (8 July at Hardwicke Bay, Yorke Peninsula); a southern giant petrel (10 July at Emu Bay, Kangaroo Island); a northern giant petrel (10 July at Port Vincent, Yorke Peninsula); three greater crested terns (10 July at Robe, Limestone Coast; 26 July at Semaphore, metro Adelaide; and 26 July at Robe, Limestone Coast); seven greater crested terns (28 July at Cape Jaffa, Port MacDonnell and Southend, Lower South East); and a giant petrel (30 July at Port Lincoln, Eyre Peninsula).A further 24 suspected H5 bird flu detections are undergoing further confirmatory testing at the Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness in Victoria.The strain of virus is consistent with the strain detected in the Southern Indian Ocean Sub-Antarctic Territories, including Heard Island.This strain has not been detected in poultry and has not become established in any part of Australia.Up-to-date national information is available at birdflu.gov.au.Although the official numbers remain reassuring low (n=29), they undoubtedly represent only a small fraction of actual H5 burden on wildlife in Australia. Two weeks ago, we looked at the growing gap between reported events, prioritized and investigated cases, and lab testing in Western Australia. Graphic generated by GeminiI've not seen an update from WA since July 17th - where total reports then exceeded 1,800 - and sadly, other states have not provided this sort of granular detail. But it is a fairly safe assumption that similar backlogs exist around the nation. Obviously, no surveillance and testing program can hope to capture more than a small fraction of the HPAI activity in birds or animals in the wild. At best, it can give us some idea as to the spread, intensity, and host range of HPAI H5 across the continent. And right now, based on available data, H5N1 appears to be making significant inroads down under. Wednesday, July 29, 2026 EID Journal Dispatch: Seroprevalence of Influenza A(H5N1) Virus in Domestic Cats at Epicenter of Dairy Cattle Outbreaks, California, USA, 2024–2026 Seropositive cats around HPAI Infected Dairy Farm#19,268We've known for more than 2 decades that cats - both large and small - are susceptible to HPAI H5 infection (see 2004 CIDRAP Report) and have seen scattered reports over the years (see 2015's HPAI H5: Catch As Cats Can).Until relatively recently, those reports were fairly rare, and mainly came from zoo animals fed on a diet of raw chicken. But since the emergence of a new, more transmissible clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus in 2021, the number of companion animals (and other mammals) reported to be infected has risen sharply.While undoubtedly underreported, more than 20% of all of the mammalian wildlife detections reported in the United States (180 of 813 USDA reports) over the past 4 years have been among felines. Many have been reported in and around dairy and poultry farms (see EID Journal: HPAI A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Domestic Dairy Cattle and Cats, United States, 2024).While many cats infected with HPAI sicken and die, others - based on seroprevalence studies (see Eurosurveillance: (HPAI) H5 virus Exposure in Domestic & Rural Stray Cats, the Netherlands, October 2020 to June 2023) - are likely only mildly affected and survive.Previously, we've seen evidence of cattle-to-bird-to-cat transmission of avian flu, large outbreaks in animal shelters suggesting cat-to-cat transmission (H7N2), and limited evidence of cat-to-human transmission (see here and here). All of which brings us to a new dispatch, published yesterday in the EID Journal, which reports a 25% seropositivity rate among (n=12) cats sampled within 2 km of infected dairy farms, while no cats were seropositive further away (n=61).While this is just one small, geographically limited, study the authors state: "Proximity to dairy farms in counties experiencing outbreaks may be a risk factor for H5N1 spillover to indoor and outdoor domestic cats."I've only posted the highlights, follow the link to read the report in its entirety.Volume 32, Number 9—September 2026DispatchSeroprevalence of Influenza A(H5N1) Virus in Domestic Cats at Epicenter of Dairy Cattle Outbreaks, California, USA, 2024–2026 Ian G. Bemis, Ismaila Shittu, Jacob F. Gomez, Esther A. Fadaka, Sofia Perez, Gregory C. Gray, and Kristen K. Coleman AbstractWe conducted a serologic study of domestic cats near the epicenter of the dairy cattle outbreaks of influenza A(H5N1) in California, USA. Three of the 12 cats sampled within 2 km of farms had neutralizing antibodies against H5N1 virus. Proximity to dairy farms was a statistically significant risk factor for seropositivity.(SNIP) Although several US dairy industry–related outbreaks of H5N1 among cats have been reported, the resulting seroprevalence of H5N1 virus among domestic cats near affected dairy farms is unknown. Therefore, we performed a serosurvey of domestic cats at the epicenter of the 2024–2025 dairy cattle outbreaks in California’s Central Valley.(SNIP)During December 2024–March 2026, we collected 73 serum samples from indoor and outdoor cats (Figure 1) within 9.7 km (6 miles) of >1 dairy farms (mean 4.7 km [2.9 miles]). Among the 73 cats, 3 tested positive for both influenza A virus nucleoprotein antibodies and neutralizing antibodies against H5 clade 2.3.4.4b. One indoor-only and 1 outdoor feral cat had neutralizing antibody titers of 1:160, and 1 indoor-only cat had a titer of 1:640, indicating strong positivity and 100% agreement between the ELISA and microneutralization assay. All negative samples had titers of <1:20. Three (25%) of the 12 cats sampled within 2 km (1.24 miles) of dairy farms were seropositive for H5N1 virus (Figure 2), yielding an overall seropositivity rate of 4.1% for all surveyed cats. Seropositive cats had a mean distance to the nearest dairy farm of 1.34 km (0.8 miles), compared with 4.83 km (3 miles) for seronegative cats (p = 0.014) (Figure 3). Average age of surveyed cats was ≈1.6 years (range ≈3 months–4.9 years); 60% were female and 40% male. Age and sex were not significantly different for seropositive and seronegative cats. Of the 73 cats surveyed, 68 (93%) were in rural areas and 5 (7%) in urban areas. All seropositive cats were in rural areas. No indoor cats were fed raw meat or dairy. (SNIP)ConclusionsAvian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b is an emerging threat to domestic cats and public health. We report a 25% seropositivity rate for the virus among domestic cats within 2 km (1.2 miles) of dairy farms in the epicenter of the H5N1 cattle outbreaks in California during 2024–2026. Proximity to dairy farms in counties experiencing outbreaks may be a risk factor for H5N1 spillover to indoor and outdoor domestic cats. Our research provides insight into potential H5N1 virus sources and transmission routes among domestic cats in the United States, for which data are scarce. Our results may help refine public health guidance on the prevention of avian influenza in cats and set the stage for future studies.Although only 3 seropositive cats were identified in our study, their closer proximity to dairy farms compared with seronegative cats is an important epidemiologic finding. (SNIP) Our study highlights a critical gap in companion animal surveillance and might be helpful to health agencies as they seek approaches to mitigating this emerging infectious disease threat. Proximity to dairy farms was a risk factor for H5N1 spillover to cats in our study. However, cattle-to-cat transmission of H5N1 virus is a relatively new phenomenon, and most cat infections reported in the literature over the past 20 years have been from bird-to-cat transmission (1). To assess the in situ risk for human-adapted reassortant influenza viruses emerging in cats, future work is needed to characterize the seroprevalence of human influenza viruses in cats and avian influenza viruses in cats near outbreaks in poultry and wild birds. Cat surveillance studies also could provide insight into nearby H5N1 outbreaks that have yet to be discovered, fully investigated, or contained. While there remains no evidence of any mass mortalities at this point in time, we do expect with this local transmission that there will be further detections in Australian wildlife." - From Transcript of remarks by Agriculture Minister Julie Collins#19,267Overnight South Australia updated their avian flu web portal, announcing that another 11 presumed positive samples have been sent to CSIRO for confirmation and genetic testing. The results of those tests also strongly suggest local transmission of the virus has occurred among native birds. Although disappointing, none of this is particularly surprising. The history with HPAI H5 - particularly since the emergence and subsequent evolution of the 2.3.4.4x clade - has been that it travels well in migratory birds, and that when it reaches new territories, it often finds suitable native hosts.While the situation in Australia continues to evolve, so far there are no reports of spillovers into poultry. On Monday I shared an X/Twitter post by Professor Raina Macintyre showing the recent H5N1 detections overlaid on a map of Australia's poultry production regions.Yesterday, the above mentioned data was published in a preprint on bioRxiv.HPAI H5N1 risk in Australia: a model for the prediction of poultry outbreaksPan Zhang, Samsung Lim, Ashley Quigley, C Raina MacIntyredoi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.27.740638This article is a preprint and has not been certified by peer review Preview PDFAbstractThe panzootic highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus has now been detected on the Australian mainland, with incursions from the sub-Antarctic region posing an increasing threat to domestic wildlife and poultry populations. Our study aimed to predict the risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks across Australia at the local government area (LGA) level using a range of influential risk factors.We first used a Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model to estimate the environmental suitability for HPAI H5N1 occurrence across Australia. The resulting suitability layer was then integrated with five additional predictor layers, including abundance data for two Southern Ocean wild birds, one of which has introduced HPAI H5N1 into Australia; abundance data for 28 native Australian wild birds; native bird flyways across Australia; Australian chicken density; and poultry farm density. The six layers were aggregated and averaged to generate an HPAI H5N1 risk map for poultry outbreaks across Australian LGAs.Although most incursions have occurred in Western Australia (WA) and South Australia (SA), we identified New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria (VIC) as having the highest predicted risk of HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks. Additional high-risk areas were identified in WA, SA, and Tasmania (TAS).In contrast, the Northern Territory (NT) and large parts of Queensland (QLD), WA, and SA were predicted to be at low risk. papers.title: Antigen clade matching enhances protective efficacy of H5N1 DNA vaccines delivered by electroporation or lipid nanoparticles 2267127
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIs) continue to threaten both agriculture and human health. Recent H5N1 clades have caused zoonotic infections in humans with mortality rates approaching 50%. However, currently licensed H5 vaccines are based on ancestral strains and may provide suboptimal protection against circulating variants. Rapidly adaptable DNA vaccine platforms offer a promising approach for clade-specific protection. Methods Codon-optimized plasmid DNA vaccines expressing hemagglutinin (HA) from two recently circulating H5N1 clades (2.3.2.1c and 2.3.4.4b) were generated and delivered by either intramuscular electroporation (EP) or a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation. Cellular and humoral responses were evaluated by multiparameter flow cytometry and ELISpot and by ELISA and pseudovirus neutralization, respectively. Protective efficacy was evaluated in lethal H5N1 murine challenge models. Results EP delivery of clade 2.3.2.1c HA (pCamb) elicited strong humoral and cellular responses and achieved complete protection against homologous viral challenge, but only partial protection against heterologous 2.3.4.4b challenge. In contrast, vaccination with clade 2.3.4.4b HA (pMich) DNA supported robust immune responses and full protection against contemporary clade challenge. Co-immunization with both plasmids via EP induced broad binding and neutralizing antibodies and conferred complete protection from clade 2.3.4.4b challenge. Moreover, formulation of the pMich plasmid optimized LNPs generated durable, protective immunity following a single dose, effective at both acute and memory timepoints. Conclusion These studies demonstrate that antigenic clade-matching is likely critical for protection against H5N1 and suggest that currently stockpiled H5N1 vaccines may not protect against contemporary viruses. Further this data suggests that DNA vaccine platforms including EP or LNP formulations can provide a flexible approach for rapid adaptation to evolving influenza strains. Funding Source NIH NIAID CIVICs Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

papers.title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

papers.title_zh: 针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的牛顿差分优化
papers.source_body_en: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.
papers.abstract_zh: 禽流感 A/H9N2 造成持续的人畜共患病和兽医威胁,但用于 抗病毒药物 化合物优先级排序的有效计算工具仍然不发达,特别是在高维神经筛选中的​​优化器行为方面。本研究提出了牛顿除差(NDD)优化,这是一种轻量级正对角曲率感知训练策略,作为针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的新型优化器,目的是评估其在对齐的分子指纹表示和化学结构验证协议中的性能。由 615 种候选活性化合物和 844 种诱饵组成的 1,459 个分子的对齐基准由 EState(79 个特征)、PubChem(881 个特征)和 Klekota–Roth(4,860 个特征)指纹代表,共享相同的分子身份、标签和分割分配。固定多层感知器 (MLP) 分类器使用 NDD 和七个基线优化器在分层、支架键和相似性聚类分割协议下跨五个重复种子进行训练。NDD 在支架密钥和相似性聚类协议下的 Klekota–Roth 指纹上实现了最高的描述性 ROC-AUC(接收者操作特征 - 曲线下面积)和 PR-AUC(曲线下精确召回面积),并且在分层分割下保持竞争力,ROC-AUC 为 0.9872。架构敏感性测试证实了跨多种网络配置的稳定 NDD 性能,ROC-AUC 值范围为 0.9876 至 0.9890。与无 Hessian 优化相比,在相同的仅 CPU 配置下,NDD 将 Klekota-Roth 上的每次运行时间从大约 50-54 秒减少到大约 8 秒,同时实现了相当的排名性能。这项工作的新颖性在于首次系统评估 H9N2 神经虚拟筛选的 NDD,证明正对角线曲率感知缩放在稀疏高维配体筛选设置中提供了实用、稳定且计算高效的优化替代方案,尽管在实际 抗病毒药物 优先级排序之前仍然需要外部验证和前瞻性实验确认。

papers.title: Activating laboratory surveillance response to the threat of H5N1 influenza in the Veterans Health Administration, 2024–25
papers.abstract: Introduction The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) mobilized and adapted its established national infrastructure to enhance influenza surveillance during 2024–2025 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) panzootic. Additionally, VHA's Public Health Reference Laboratory (PHRL) expanded capacity for H5 subtyping and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to support detection. Methods Routine influenza surveillance was enhanced with customized queries to identify cases in high-risk counties with reported H5N1 detected in animals. In coordination with VHA clinical laboratories, select samples were sent to PHRL. PHRL subtyped specimens received, which included hospitalized cases. Demographics of influenza A cases in VHA were compared with those residing in high-risk “surveilled” counties (with reported H5N1 detection in animals) and those whose specimens were sent to PHRL for H5 subtyping. Results From 4/1/2024-5/31/2025, we identified 40,406 positive influenza A VHA cases (12.5% with local subtyping performed), including 5,348 cases from “surveilled” counties. A total of 1,155 specimens were received by PHRL for H5 subtyping and 180 completed WGS. Cases from “surveilled” counties had fewer females, fewer in 50–69 age group and more of Hispanic ethnicity compared to other influenza A cases. No H5N1 was detected. Conclusion We highlight the complexity and resources necessary for epidemiologic and laboratory surveillance of H5N1 within a large, national health system during a recognized panzootic. Additional resources for decentralized influenza A subtyping at local VA clinical laboratories are needed as centralized subtyping and WGS at PHRL was not comprehensive. Although H5 influenza has not yet been observed among Veterans within VHA, the ongoing risk warrants continued vigilance and monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) enhanced its influenza surveillance infrastructure during the 2024–2025 HPAI A(H5N1) panzootic by expanding laboratory capacity for H5 subtyping and whole genome sequencing. Despite receiving 1,155 specimens for H5 subtyping and completing 180 whole genome sequences, no H5N1 was detected. The study underscores the complexity and resources required for surveillance in a large health system, emphasizing the need for continued vigilance and decentralized subtyping capabilities to improve coverage.

papers.title_zh: 激活实验室 监测 对退伍军人健康管理局 H5N1 流感威胁的响应,2024-25
papers.source_body_en: Introduction The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) mobilized and adapted its established national infrastructure to enhance influenza surveillance during 2024–2025 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) panzootic. Additionally, VHA's Public Health Reference Laboratory (PHRL) expanded capacity for H5 subtyping and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to support detection. Methods Routine influenza surveillance was enhanced with customized queries to identify cases in high-risk counties with reported H5N1 detected in animals. In coordination with VHA clinical laboratories, select samples were sent to PHRL. PHRL subtyped specimens received, which included hospitalized cases. Demographics of influenza A cases in VHA were compared with those residing in high-risk “surveilled” counties (with reported H5N1 detection in animals) and those whose specimens were sent to PHRL for H5 subtyping. Results From 4/1/2024-5/31/2025, we identified 40,406 positive influenza A VHA cases (12.5% with local subtyping performed), including 5,348 cases from “surveilled” counties. A total of 1,155 specimens were received by PHRL for H5 subtyping and 180 completed WGS. Cases from “surveilled” counties had fewer females, fewer in 50–69 age group and more of Hispanic ethnicity compared to other influenza A cases. No H5N1 was detected. Conclusion We highlight the complexity and resources necessary for epidemiologic and laboratory surveillance of H5N1 within a large, national health system during a recognized panzootic. Additional resources for decentralized influenza A subtyping at local VA clinical laboratories are needed as centralized subtyping and WGS at PHRL was not comprehensive. Although H5 influenza has not yet been observed among Veterans within VHA, the ongoing risk warrants continued vigilance and monitoring.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of PB2 mutations associated with mammalian adaptation of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza viruses
papers.abstract: The highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) subtype H5N1 has been continuously circulating among wild bird populations and domestic poultry. It’s ongoing circulation has led to outbreaks in poultry and U.S. dairy cattle populations, as well as sporadic severe infections in individuals engaged in poultry and dairy farming. These occurrences have raised concerns about the potential evolution of this virus into a pandemic strain. To elucidate the molecular determinants facilitating H5N1 cross-species adaptation and to evaluate its implications for public health, we conducted serials of sequence analysis and specific-site mutations on the viral polymerase subunit PB2 to determine its effect on polymerase activity and viral infectivity. The results showed that three mutations in the PB2 protein (E362G, D441N and M631L) were presented cooperative effects associated with enhanced viral replication in mammalian cells. Compared to the original isolated strain of the 2.3.4.4b clade, A/chicken/NL/FAV-0033/2021, these three mutations were predominantly identified in isolates obtained from cattle and other mammalian hosts between 2021 and 2024. The M631L mutation, identified as the primary determinant of increased polymerase activity in mammalian cells, significantly enhanced the binding affinity of PB2 to ANP32A. The mutation E362G and D441N did not increased polymerase activity and viral replication significantly but enhanced binding affinity of PB2 to ANP32A. The combined mutations with E362G, D441N and M631L resulted in a significantly increased polymerase activity and viral replication in H5N1 virus, and significantly elevated viral loads and aggravated pulmonary pathology in lungs of mice with H5N1 infection. These findings indicate that the PB2-M631L mutation constitutes a crucial molecular marker for the adaptation of H5N1 to mammalian hosts, whereas the E362G and D441N mutations likely function as supportive modulatory factors that optimize this host-adaptation process.

papers.title_zh: 与哺乳动物适应高致病性 H5N1 禽流感 病毒相关的 PB2 突变 的鉴定和表征
papers.source_body_en: The highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) subtype H5N1 has been continuously circulating among wild bird populations and domestic poultry. It’s ongoing circulation has led to outbreaks in poultry and U.S. dairy cattle populations, as well as sporadic severe infections in individuals engaged in poultry and dairy farming. These occurrences have raised concerns about the potential evolution of this virus into a pandemic strain. To elucidate the molecular determinants facilitating H5N1 cross-species adaptation and to evaluate its implications for public health, we conducted serials of sequence analysis and specific-site mutations on the viral polymerase subunit PB2 to determine its effect on polymerase activity and viral infectivity. The results showed that three mutations in the PB2 protein (E362G, D441N and M631L) were presented cooperative effects associated with enhanced viral replication in mammalian cells. Compared to the original isolated strain of the 2.3.4.4b clade, A/chicken/NL/FAV-0033/2021, these three mutations were predominantly identified in isolates obtained from cattle and other mammalian hosts between 2021 and 2024. The M631L mutation, identified as the primary determinant of increased polymerase activity in mammalian cells, significantly enhanced the binding affinity of PB2 to ANP32A. The mutation E362G and D441N did not increased polymerase activity and viral replication significantly but enhanced binding affinity of PB2 to ANP32A. The combined mutations with E362G, D441N and M631L resulted in a significantly increased polymerase activity and viral replication in H5N1 virus, and significantly elevated viral loads and aggravated pulmonary pathology in lungs of mice with H5N1 infection. These findings indicate that the PB2-M631L mutation constitutes a crucial molecular marker for the adaptation of H5N1 to mammalian hosts, whereas the E362G and D441N mutations likely function as supportive modulatory factors that optimize this host-adaptation process.

papers.title: Genetic and Pathogenicity Studies of Avian Influenza (H9N2) Virus Isolated from Chickens in Jiangsu Province, China, in 2025
papers.abstract: In this study, one H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus (AIV) was isolated in Jiangsu Province, China, in March 2025. According to phylogenetic analysis, the HA gene fragment of the H9N2 isolate was classified as the B4.7 lineage, with the remaining seven segments falling into the Eurasian lineage. This H9N2 virus underwent complex genetic reassortment across multiple regions in China during its evolution, and key amino acid substitutions were identified, which may enhance its viral polymerase activity and replication efficiency in mice. Critically, a mouse experiment demonstrated that the H9N2 virus replicated effectively in the lungs and nasal turbinates of BALB/c mice without requiring prior adaptation. In addition, poultry infection studies showed that the H9N2 virus could replicate and spread more efficiently in chickens than in ducks. Moreover, the virus could be transmitted to contacted ducks through infected chickens with greater efficiency than from ducks to ducks. Furthermore, in the lungs of inoculated chickens and ducks, the mRNA expression levels of pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs) and cytokines were upregulated, while the overall fold increase in ducks was lower than that in chickens. In conclusion, these results highlighted the potential public health risk presented by chicken-derived H9N2 AIV, emphasizing the critical need for enhanced routine surveillance of H9N2 AIVs from poultry.

elements_zh.methods: 对 H9N2 病毒进行系统发育分析以确定其谱系,并在中国多个地区检查了基因重排。进行小鼠和家禽感染研究以评估复制效率和 传播 动态。
elements_zh.main_results: 小鼠实验表明,H9N2病毒无需事先适应即可在BALB/c小鼠的肺部和鼻甲中有效复制。家禽感染研究表明,该病毒在鸡中的复制和传播效率比在鸭中更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,鸡源性 H9N2 病毒在小鼠体内的复制效率有所提高,并且由于其在家禽物种之间有效 传播 的潜力,可能会造成公共健康风险。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了在家禽中监测 H9N2 禽流感 病毒的重要性,以更好地了解其感染人畜共患 传播 的潜力,并为 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到动物模型使用的限制,可能无法完全反映人类感染动态。证据是温和的,因为研究结果是基于实验数据而不是现场观察。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genetic characteristics and pathogenic potential of an H9N2 avian influenza virus isolated from chickens in Jiangsu Province, China, in 2025, to assess its public health risk.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved isolating an H9N2 avian influenza virus from chickens in Jiangsu Province, China, in March 2025, and analyzing its genetic evolution and pathogenicity through mouse and poultry infection experiments.
analysis_en.methods: The H9N2 virus was subjected to phylogenetic analysis to determine its lineage, and genetic reassortment was examined across multiple regions in China. Mouse and poultry infection studies were conducted to assess replication efficiency and transmission dynamics.
analysis_en.main_results: A mouse experiment showed that the H9N2 virus replicated effectively in the lungs and nasal turbinates of BALB/c mice without prior adaptation. Poultry infection studies revealed that the virus replicated and spread more efficiently in chickens than in ducks.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the chicken-derived H9N2 virus has enhanced replication efficiency in mice and may pose a public health risk due to its potential for efficient transmission between poultry species.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of monitoring H9N2 avian influenza viruses in poultry to better understand their potential for zoonotic transmission and to inform surveillance strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of animal models, which may not fully reflect human infection dynamics. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on experimental data rather than field observations.

papers.title_zh: 2025年从中国江苏省鸡中分离的禽流感(H9N2)病毒的遗传和致病性研究
papers.source_body_en: In this study, one H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus (AIV) was isolated in Jiangsu Province, China, in March 2025. According to phylogenetic analysis, the HA gene fragment of the H9N2 isolate was classified as the B4.7 lineage, with the remaining seven segments falling into the Eurasian lineage. This H9N2 virus underwent complex genetic reassortment across multiple regions in China during its evolution, and key amino acid substitutions were identified, which may enhance its viral polymerase activity and replication efficiency in mice. Critically, a mouse experiment demonstrated that the H9N2 virus replicated effectively in the lungs and nasal turbinates of BALB/c mice without requiring prior adaptation. In addition, poultry infection studies showed that the H9N2 virus could replicate and spread more efficiently in chickens than in ducks. Moreover, the virus could be transmitted to contacted ducks through infected chickens with greater efficiency than from ducks to ducks. Furthermore, in the lungs of inoculated chickens and ducks, the mRNA expression levels of pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs) and cytokines were upregulated, while the overall fold increase in ducks was lower than that in chickens. In conclusion, these results highlighted the potential public health risk presented by chicken-derived H9N2 AIV, emphasizing the critical need for enhanced routine surveillance of H9N2 AIVs from poultry.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究于2025年3月在中国江苏省分离到1株H9N2亚型禽流感病毒(AIV)。根据系统发育分析,H9N2分离物的HA基因片段被归类为B4.7谱系,其余7个片段属于欧亚谱系。这种H9N2病毒在进化期间在中国多个地区经历了复杂的基因重排,并确定了关键氨基酸取代,这可能会增强其病毒聚合酶活性和在小鼠中的复制效率。至关重要的是,小鼠实验证明 H9N2 病毒无需事先适应即可在 BALB/c 小鼠的肺部和鼻甲中有效复制。此外,家禽感染研究表明,H9N2病毒在鸡中的复制和传播效率比在鸭中更高。此外,病毒可以通过受感染的鸡传播给接触过的鸭子,其效率比鸭子传播给鸭子的效率更高。此外,在接种的鸡和鸭的肺部,模式识别受体(PRR)和细胞因子的mRNA表达水平上调,而鸭的总体倍数增幅低于鸡。总之,这些结果强调了鸡源性 H9N2 AIV 带来的潜在公共卫生风险,强调了对家禽 H9N2 AIV 加强常规 监测 的迫切需要。

papers.title: RfxCas13d mediates robust cross-strain suppression of highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) continue to cause substantial disease in birds and mammals, with repeated H5N1 spillovers highlighting the need for broadly protective antiviral strategies. Here, we develop a programmable RNA-targeting antiviral platform based on RfxCas13d and evaluate its activity in avian cells. Screening of five Cas13 orthologs in chicken DF1 fibroblasts revealed RfxCas13d as the most potent and well tolerated effector. Virus-specific CRISPR RNAs (crRNAs) targeting conserved regions of positive- and negative-sense influenza RNA were tested against A/WSN/033 (H1N1) and multiple HPAIV isolates, including a member of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1. Targeting positive-sense RNA conferred superior influenza inhibitory activity and was further enhanced by multiplexed crRNA expression. These findings establish RfxCas13d as a versatile RNA-guided antiviral platform and provide a foundation for cross-strain influenza control through conserved RNA targeting.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the ongoing threat of highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) by developing a broadly protective antiviral strategy. The background highlights the repeated spillovers of H5N1 and the need for antiviral approaches that can target multiple strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved developing and evaluating a programmable RNA-targeting antiviral platform using RfxCas13d in avian cells. It focused on avian influenza viruses, including H5N1, and tested the platform against multiple HPAIV isolates.
analysis.methods: The researchers screened five Cas13 orthologs in chicken DF1 fibroblasts to identify the most potent and well-tolerated effector, which was RfxCas13d. They then tested virus-specific CRISPR RNAs (crRNAs) targeting conserved regions of influenza RNA against A/WSN/033 (H1N1) and various HPAIV isolates, including a clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 member.
analysis.main_results: Screening of five Cas13 orthologs in chicken DF1 fibroblasts revealed RfxCas13d as the most potent and well-tolerated effector. The study also demonstrated that targeting positive-sense RNA conferred superior influenza inhibitory activity, which was further enhanced by multiplexed crRNA expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish RfxCas13d as a versatile RNA-guided antiviral platform capable of cross-strain suppression, offering a new approach for controlling influenza through conserved RNA targeting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide a foundation for developing antiviral strategies that can target multiple strains of avian influenza, potentially improving surveillance, diagnosis, and control of HPAIVs in both avian and mammalian hosts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro testing in avian cells, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of in vivo validation and long-term efficacy data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of RfxCas13d as a programmable RNA-targeting antiviral platform against highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs), particularly H5N1. The research highlights the need for broadly protective strategies against HPAIVs, which continue to cause significant disease in birds and mammals. The study evaluated RfxCas13d in avian cells, demonstrating its potency and tolerance. It found that targeting positive-sense RNA significantly enhanced antiviral activity, with multiplexed crRNA expression further improving effectiveness. The findings suggest that RfxCas13d could be a versatile tool for cross-strain influenza control through conserved RNA targeting. However, the study is limited to in vitro testing, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of in vivo validation and long-term data. The results have implications for improving surveillance and control of HPAIVs, particularly in avian populations, and may inform future research into RNA-based antiviral strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过制定广泛保护的 抗病毒药物 策略来解决 高致病性禽流感 病毒 (HPAIV) 的持续威胁。背景强调了 H5N1 的重复 跨物种溢出 以及对可针对多种菌株的 抗病毒药物 方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在禽类细胞中使用 RfxCas13d 开发和评估可编程 RNA 靶向 抗病毒药物 平台。它专注于 禽流感 病毒,包括 H5N1,并针对多种 HPAIV 分离株测试了该平台。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员在鸡 DF1 成纤维细胞中筛选了 5 个 Cas13 直向同源物,以确定最有效和耐受性最好的效应子,即 RfxCas13d。然后,他们测试了针对 A/WSN/033 (H1N1) 和各种 HPAIV 分离株(包括分支 2.3.4.4b H5N1 成员)的流感 RNA 保守区域的病毒特异性 CRISPR RNA (crRNA)。
elements_zh.main_results: 对鸡 DF1 成纤维细胞中五种 Cas13 直向同源物的筛选表明,RfxCas13d 是最有效且耐受性最好的效应子。该研究还表明,靶向正义 RNA 具有卓越的流感抑制活性,而多重 crRNA 表达可进一步增强这种活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,RfxCas13d 是一种多功能 RNA 引导的 抗病毒药物 平台,能够抑制交叉菌株,为通过保守 RNA 靶向控制流感提供了一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为开发 抗病毒药物 策略奠定了基础,该策略可以针对 禽流感 的多种菌株,潜在地改善 监测、诊断 以及对禽类和哺乳动物 宿主 中 HPAIV 的控制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于禽类细胞的体外测试,由于缺乏体内验证和长期疗效数据,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 高致病性禽流感 病毒 (HPAIV) 继续在鸟类和哺乳动物中引起严重疾病,H5N1 跨物种溢出 的反复出现凸显了对广泛保护性 抗病毒药物 策略的需求。在这里,我们开发了基于 RfxCas13d 的可编程 RNA 靶向 抗病毒药物 平台,并评估其在鸟类细胞中的活性。对鸡 DF1 成纤维细胞中五种 Cas13 直向同源物的筛选表明,RfxCas13d 是最有效且耐受性最好的效应子。针对 A/WSN/033 (H1N1) 和多种 HPAIV 分离株(包括分支 2.3.4.4b H5N1 的成员)测试了针对正义和负义流感 RNA 保守区域的病毒特异性 CRISPR RNA (crRNA)。靶向正义 RNA 具有优异的流感抑制活性,并且通过多重 crRNA 表达进一步增强。这些发现将 RfxCas13d 确立为多功能 RNA 引导的 抗病毒药物 平台,并为通过保守 RNA 靶向控制跨毒株流感奠定了基础。
