elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5 病毒对人类和动物健康构成持续的人畜共患威胁,因此需要在新出现的 暴发 期间快速部署广泛的保护性对策。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用计算流程设计了鼠抗 H5 单克隆抗体 (5C2) 的人源化变体,并在将 DNA 递送至野生型小鼠后评估了它们的体内表达和功能。
elements_zh.methods: 将 BioPhi 与内部精炼相结合的计算管道生成了鼠 5C2 抗体的人源化变体,然后针对体内表达进行了优化,并通过注射和体内电穿孔将其作为 DNA 编码的单克隆抗体 (DMAb) 递送给小鼠。
elements_zh.main_results: DMAb 处理小鼠的血清对多个 H5N1 进化枝(包括当前流行的进化枝 2.3.4.4b 病毒)表现出强烈的结合和假病毒中和作用,并且在构建体中观察到持续的抗体表达数月。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,优化的计算机人源化保留了关键的功能特性,包括针对不同的 H5N1 进化枝的交叉反应性,并且计算工作流程能够快速生成具有针对新兴威胁的广泛活性的人源化抗体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持 DNA 编码的人源化抗体作为大流行防范平台的潜力,能够通过持续的交叉反应免疫快速应对季节性或大流行性流感威胁。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外结合和假病毒中和测定以及小鼠体内表达,这使得针对人类不同循环毒株的临床疗效、安全性和性能存在不确定性。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 H5 亚型的 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 对人类和动物健康构成持续的人畜共患威胁。广泛中和抗体 (bnAb) 为大流行防范提供了强大的工具,但转化为临床通常需要人源化,以避免针对鼠抗体的免疫反应,这通常会影响其在不同病毒株中的功能。方法 我们开发了一个计算管道,将 BioPhi 与内部改进相结合,以生成 5C2 的人源化变体,5C2 是一种针对进化枝 2.3.2.1 H5N1 病毒的鼠抗体。为了评估人源化抗体是否可以保留亲本克隆的广度和效力,我们设计了一组独特的人源化构建体,并将它们与 VH/VL 嵌合体和鼠野生型 mAb 进行比较,这些构建体都针对体内表达进行了遗传优化。结果我们确认了所有构建体的体外表达,随后通过注射和体内电穿孔 (EP) 将它们作为 DNA 编码的单克隆抗体 (DMAb) 递送给野生型小鼠。DMAb 处理小鼠的血清表现出与多个 H5N1 进化枝的强结合和假病毒中和作用,包括目前流行的泛动物进化枝 2.3.4.4b 病毒。体内 DMAb 递送支持跨构建体的持续表达数月。结论 这些数据表明,优化的计算机人源化可以保留关键的功能特性,包括针对多个进化枝的交叉反应性。我们的结果支持使用这种计算工作流程来快速生成具有广泛活性的人源化抗体,突出了其针对新出现的季节性或大流行威胁的潜在应用。资金来源 NIH/NIAID CIVIC (75N93019C00051) 主题类别 疫苗 和免疫治疗 (VAC)

papers.full_text: Introduction The Women in Avian Physiology: 2025 is the third research topic in the Frontiers Avian Physiology section focused on women. The objective of this series is to help promote avian physiology research being led by women who are especially early in their careers. Submissions are welcomed from all areas of Avian Physiology. In the 2025 topic, 9 papers were accepted covering the areas of Immunity and the Microbiome, Satellite Cells and Extracellular Matrix, Skeletal Integrity and Eggshell Production, Stress, and Avian Influenza. Immunity and the microbiome Dasireddy et al. studied the use of symbiotics to regulate the cecal microbiota in chickens through enhancing the growth of beneficial bacteria to limit the negative effects of mycotoxins found in feed and to improve the immune response. Chronic ingestion of mycotoxins impacts intestinal function. They found that synbiotic supplementation on day 35 in chickens increased mucosal immunity and modified microbial composition and fermentation profiles. This is a first step in the research to develop in vivo microbial detoxification strategies to improve gut health. Nabthonglang et al. and colleagues studied the effect of bardoxolone methyl on the lower reproductive tract microbiome in turkey breeder hens. In turkeys, fertility declines with age due to reduced sperm storage in the uterovaginal junction from oxidative stress, inflammation and aging. Bardoxolone methyl reduces both inflammation and oxidative stress. Their results showed that bardoxolone methyl treatment enhanced energy metabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis, and stress resilience without altering microbial diversity but may fine-tune mucosal microbial communities in the uterovaginal junction. Many wild bird populations are in decline from environmental changes. Krama et al. researched the blood microbiome in wintering greenfinches before and during an outbreak of trichomonosis. Prior to the outbreak no bacterial contamination was found in the blood. Interestingly greenfinches with irregular food access had lower bacterial contamination in their blood compared to birds with permanent food access. Thus, feeding accessibility affects microbial contamination, and may play a role in the physiological resilience in wild birds. Satellite cells and extracellular matrix A review article by Yimiletey et al. discussed how intense genetic selection in commercial poultry has increased growth rate, breast muscle mass, and production efficiency. The satellite cell is responsible for all posthatch muscle growth. With genetic selection the satellite cell population has changed in its cellular properties of proliferation and differentiation as well as molecular profiles and heterogeneity. These changes in the satellite cell population in commercial birds may significantly contribute to the development of breast muscle myopathies including wooden breast. Further defining satellite cell biology will benefit commercial poultry production systems. Wooden breast in broilers is characterized by the fibrosis of the breast muscle. The transmembrane proteoglycan, syndecan-4, is a key regulator of satellite cell and fibroblast proliferation. Pejšková et al. have found through the over expression of syndecan-4 in fibroblasts that it may be a modulator of the fibrotic response in chickens. Skeletal integrity and eggshell production Keel bone fractures and deviations are an animal welfare issue in laying hens. Fractures of the keel bone lead to reduced mobility and egg laying. Hildebrand et al. compared keel bone traits and eggshell production in a hybrid layer line and two non-egg laying chicken genotypes. They found that earlier onset of egg laying in the hybrid layer line did not correspond with earlier maturation of the keel bone. The delayed maturation of the keel bone in the hybrid layer line in relation to eggshell production could increase susceptibility to fractures of the keel bone. Leskovec et al. reported on the effects of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) and heat stress on the morphology and geometry of the tibiotarsal growth plate in Ross 308 broilers. Interestingly, high PUFA dietary supplementation induced morphometric changes in the growth plate that were similar to tibial dyschondroplasia. Heat stress reduced the crude ash content and biomechanics of the tibiotarsal growth plate. Adding antioxidant supplementation to the feed negated the effects of high PUFA levels and heat stress. Taken together, these findings may lead to the development of nutritional strategies to improve broiler bone health. Stress Pierzchala-Koziec et al. showed that not only does stress induce increased plasma concentrations of Met-enkephalin in chickens but also peripheral administered Met-enkephalin depressed the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA) axis activity during restraint stress. Thus, it is proposed that endogenous Met-enkephalin modulates the activity of the HPA axis. Avian influenza Infection with avian influenza virus can negatively impact reproduction in turkey breeder hens. Kosonsiriluk et al. reported on the early transcriptomic response to low-pathogenic strain avian influenza infection in the vagina and uterovaginal junction. In the vagina, 701 genes were differentially expressed in symptomatic vs. presymptomatic birds. Pathways affected in symptomatic turkey hens included those associated with protein synthesis, metabolism energy production, and vascular development. In the uterovaginal junction pathways involved in cellular maintenance and metabolism were affected. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to promote avian physiology research led by women, particularly those early in their careers, by compiling a series of papers focused on various aspects of avian biology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This editorial introduces a research topic consisting of 9 accepted papers covering areas such as immunity, microbiome, satellite cells, skeletal integrity, stress, and avian influenza in avian species.
analysis.methods: The editorial summarizes findings from multiple studies, including experiments on symbiotics in chickens, bardoxolone methyl in turkey breeder hens, blood microbiome in greenfinches, genetic selection in poultry, and avian influenza infection in turkeys.
analysis.main_results: Key findings include increased mucosal immunity and modified microbial composition in chickens with synbiotic supplementation, enhanced energy metabolism and stress resilience in turkeys treated with bardoxolone methyl, and altered pathways in turkey hens infected with low-pathogenic avian influenza.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as steps toward developing strategies for improving gut health, reproductive function, and bone health in avian species, with novel insights into microbial detoxification and stress modulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform potential nutritional and therapeutic interventions for avian health, contributing to improved welfare, production efficiency, and disease management in poultry and wild birds.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the editorial summarizes multiple studies without providing original data, and the limitations are not explicitly discussed in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial introduces the 'Women in Avian Physiology: 2025' research topic, featuring 9 papers on immunity, microbiome, satellite cells, skeletal integrity, stress, and avian influenza. Key findings include synbiotic supplementation enhancing mucosal immunity in chickens, bardoxolone methyl improving metabolic function in turkeys, and altered pathways in avian influenza-infected hens. The work highlights novel strategies for gut health, reproductive function, and bone health, with implications for avian welfare and production. The evidence strength is moderate, as the editorial summarizes existing studies without original data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过编写一系列专注于鸟类生物学各个方面的论文,促进由女性,特别是处于职业生涯早期的女性领导的鸟类生理学研究。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这篇社论介绍了一个由 9 篇已接受论文组成的研究主题,涵盖鸟类物种的免疫、微生物组、卫星细胞、骨骼完整性、压力和 禽流感 等领域。
elements_zh.methods: 该社论总结了多项研究的结果,包括鸡的共生实验、火鸡种母鸡的甲基巴多索隆、绿翅雀的血液微生物组、家禽的遗传选择以及火鸡的 禽流感 感染。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要发现包括补充合生元可提高鸡的粘膜免疫力并改变微生物组成,用甲基巴多索隆治疗的火鸡可增强能量代谢和应激恢复能力,以及感染低致病性 禽流感 的火鸡母鸡的途径发生改变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为制定改善鸟类肠道健康、生殖功能和骨骼健康策略的步骤,并对微生物解毒和应激调节提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为禽类健康的潜在营养和治疗干预措施提供了信息,有助于改善家禽和 野生鸟类 的福利、生产效率和疾病管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为社论总结了多项研究,但没有提供原始数据,并且所提供的证据中没有明确讨论其局限性。

papers.title: Intranasal administration of a pan-reactive influenza antibody reveals Fc-independent mode of protection 2259232
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Monoclonal antibodies protect through two core mechanisms: their antigen-binding fragment (Fab) directly binds and neutralizes viral antigens, while the fragment crystallizable domain (Fc) engages Fcγ receptors to activate immune effector functions. We investigated and segregated the relative contribution of each antibody domain to immune protection by comparing peripheral/systemic versus local/mucosal delivery within a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus Methods We performed intranasal versus intravenous delivery of CR9114, the broadest known human influenza antibody, which engages a conserved epitope on the hemagglutinin stem to provide protection against both influenza A and influenza B viruses within pre-clinical challenge models. Mice received either wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone (no Fc domain) 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses. Survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50). Results Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yam and B/Vic compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold. Systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats. The F(ab’)2 fragment alone conferred full prophylaxis when delivered locally but was ineffective systemically. Conclusion These findings reveal that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection. Local mucosal delivery achieves potent Fc-independent immunity, which was also seen in the absence of conventional neutralization activity, offering a new strategy for antibody-based prevention of influenza and other respiratory infections. Funding Source Leyden Laboratories B.V. Topic Categories Mucosal and Regional Immunology (MUC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate and segregate the relative contribution of antibody domains to immune protection against influenza virus by comparing peripheral/systemic versus local/mucosal delivery in a mouse model.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus, comparing intranasal versus intravenous delivery of the broadest known human influenza antibody CR9114 against multiple influenza strains.
analysis.methods: Mice received wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses; survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50).
analysis.main_results: Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yamagata, and B/Victoria compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold; systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection, with local mucosal delivery achieving potent Fc-independent immunity even in the absence of conventional neutralization activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local mucosal delivery offers a new strategy for antibody-based prevention of influenza and other respiratory infections, potentially enhancing protection against diverse strains including avian influenza A/H5N1.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on pre-clinical challenge models in mice, and while the findings are robust within this context, further studies are needed to confirm efficacy in humans; the evidence strength is moderate due to the limited translational scope.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relative contribution of antibody domains to immune protection against influenza virus by comparing intranasal versus intravenous delivery of the broad-spectrum antibody CR9114 in mice. Results showed that intranasal delivery significantly increased potency against multiple influenza strains, including A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yamagata, and B/Victoria, compared to intravenous administration. Systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, but intranasal protection remained effective even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats, including the F(ab’)2 fragment alone. These findings demonstrate that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection, with local mucosal delivery achieving potent Fc-independent immunity, offering a novel strategy for preventing influenza and other respiratory infections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过比较小鼠模型中的外周/全身与局部/粘膜递送,研究和分离抗体结构域对流感病毒免疫保护的相对贡献。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在针对流感病毒的抗体预防的小鼠模型中进行的,比较了针对多种流感病毒株的最广泛已知的人类流感抗体 CR9114 的鼻内和静脉内递送。
elements_zh.methods: 小鼠在甲型/H1N1、A/H3N2、A/H5N1、B/Yamagata 或 B/Victoria 流感病毒致死攻击前 24 小时单独接受野生型 CR9114、Fc 沉默突变体(LALA、N297Q)或二价抗原结合 F(ab’)2 片段;测量存活率和体重变化以确定保护作用和中位有效剂量(ED50)。
elements_zh.main_results: 与静脉内给药相比,鼻内给药 CR9114 导致抗致命性流感 A/H1N1、A/H5N1、A/H3N2、B/Yamagata 和 B/Victoria 的效力增加高达 50 倍;全身保护需要完整的 Fc 结构域,而即使采用 Fc 沉默或 Fc 耗尽的形式,鼻内保护仍然很强。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,抗体递送途径决定了其保护机制,即使在缺乏常规中和活性的情况下,局部粘膜递送也能实现有效的 Fc 独立免疫。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 局部粘膜递送为基于抗体的流感和其他呼吸道感染的预防提供了一种新策略,可能增强对包括 禽流感 A/H5N1 在内的多种毒株的保护。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于小鼠的临床前挑战模型,虽然在这方面的研究结果是可靠的,但还需要进一步的研究来证实对人类的功效;由于翻译范围有限,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 单克隆抗体通过两个核心机制提供保护:其抗原结合片段 (Fab) 直接结合并中和病毒抗原,而片段可结晶结构域 (Fc) 与 Fcγ 受体结合以激活免疫效应功能。我们通过比较针对流感病毒的抗体预防小鼠模型中的外周/全身与局部/粘膜递送,研究并分离了每个抗体结构域对免疫保护的相对贡献。方法我们进行了CR9114的鼻内与静脉内递送,CR9114是已知最广泛的人类流感抗体,其与血凝素茎上的保守表位结合,以在临床前挑战模型中提供针对甲型流感和乙型流感病毒的保护。在用 A/H1N1、A/H3N2、A/H5N1、B/Yamagata 或 B/Victoria 病毒致死攻击前 24 小时,小鼠接受野生型 CR9114、Fc 沉默突变体(LALA、N297Q)或单独的二价抗原结合 F(ab’)2 片段(无 Fc 结构域)。测量存活率和体重变化以确定保护作用和中位有效剂量 (ED50)。结果 与静脉内给药相比,鼻内给药 CR9114 的抗致命性流感 A/H1N1、A/H5N1、A/H3N2、B/Yam 和 B/Vic 的效力提高了 50 倍。全身保护需要完整的 Fc 结构域,而即使采用 Fc 沉默或 Fc 耗尽的形式,鼻内保护仍然很强。当局部递送时,单独的 F(ab’)2 片段可以提供充分的预防作用,但全身无效。结论这些发现揭示了抗体递送途径决定了其保护机制。局部粘膜递送实现了有效的不依赖于 Fc 的免疫,这在缺乏常规中和活性的情况下也可见到,为基于抗体的流感和其他呼吸道感染的预防提供了新策略。资金来源 Leyden Laboratories B.V. 主题类别 粘膜和区域免疫学 (MUC)

papers.title: Optimizing T Cell Priming Using TLR4/9 Combination Adjuvant For Robust Cell-Mediated Immunity Against Influenza 2307646
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Subunit vaccines are safe but rarely induce robust, long-lasting immunity, especially cell-mediated immunity (CMI). Here, we investigated the potential of IVAX-1, a combination of TLR4 (MPLA) and TLR9 (CpG 1018) agonists formulated in a squalene oil-in-water emulsion (AddaVax), to mediate protection and generate CMI. Methods We leveraged a murine H5N1 influenza model with fate-map reporters, conditional knock-out mice, multiphoton imaging, and flow cytometry to elucidate early spatiotemporal features of IVAX-1-driven immunity. Antigen-specific CMI was evaluated via ELISpot and recall assays. Results Immune priming with IVAX-1 enhanced dendritic cell (DC) maturation and recruitment of myeloid cells to the injection site, resulting in higher numbers of neutrophils, monocytes, and antigen-presenting DCs in the draining lymph node (DLN), independent of antigen clearance kinetics. This induced islands of IFN-γ+ cells in the DLN, suggesting clonal expansion. In addition, IVAX-1 generated a robust antigen-specific functional (IFN-γ+) T cell response. Deletion of Type 1 conventional DCs (XCR1+) cells abrogated IVAX-1-mediated T cell response. Furthermore, immunization with IVAX-1 generated significantly higher numbers of flu-specific memory T cells in the lungs and spleen. IVAX-1 conferred durable protection and superior viral clearance from the lungs up to 60 days after immunization. Conclusion By leveraging synergistic innate immune activation through multiple TLR pathways, the combination optimizes T cell priming without relying on antigen depot effects. Our findings identify key early innate immune events and cellular mediators that drive robust CMI and demonstrate the potential of TLR agonist combinations to elicit durable T-cell immunity. source_records.abstract: Abstract Introduction Subunit vaccines are safe but rarely induce robust, long-lasting immunity, especially cell-mediated immunity (CMI). Here, we investigated the potential of IVAX-1, a combination of TLR4 (MPLA) and TLR9 (CpG 1018) agonists formulated in a squalene oil-in-water emulsion (AddaVax), to mediate protection and generate CMI. Methods We leveraged a murine H5N1 influenza model with fate-map reporters, conditional knock-out mice, multiphoton imaging, and flow cytometry to elucidate early spatiotemporal features of IVAX-1-driven immunity. Antigen-specific CMI was evaluated via ELISpot and recall assays. Results Immune priming with IVAX-1 enhanced dendritic cell (DC) maturation and recruitment of myeloid cells to the injection site, resulting in higher numbers of neutrophils, monocytes, and antigen-presenting DCs in the draining lymph node (DLN), independent of antigen clearance kinetics. This induced islands of IFN-γ+ cells in the DLN, suggesting clonal expansion. In addition, IVAX-1 generated a robust antigen-specific functional (IFN-γ+) T cell response. Deletion of Type 1 conventional DCs (XCR1+) cells abrogated IVAX-1-mediated T cell response. Furthermore, immunization with IVAX-1 generated significantly higher numbers of flu-specific memory T cells in the lungs and spleen. IVAX-1 conferred durable protection and superior viral clearance from the lungs up to 60 days after immunization. Conclusion By leveraging synergistic innate immune activation through multiple TLR pathways, the combination optimizes T cell priming without relying on antigen depot effects. Our findings identify key early innate immune events and cellular mediators that drive robust CMI and demonstrate the potential of TLR agonist combinations to elicit durable T-cell immunity. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 亚基 疫苗 是安全的,但很少诱导强大、持久的免疫,尤其是细胞介导的免疫 (CMI)。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用鼠 H5N1 流感模型研究了 IVAX-1(在角鲨烯水包油乳液 (AddaVax) 中配制的 TLR4 (MPLA) 和 TLR9 (CpG 1018) 激动剂组合)介导保护和产生 CMI 的潜力。
elements_zh.methods: 我们利用带有命运图谱报告基因的鼠 H5N1 流感模型、条件敲除小鼠、多光子成像和流式细胞术来阐明 IVAX-1 驱动免疫的早期时空特征。通过 ELISpot 和回忆分析评估抗原特异性 CMI。
elements_zh.main_results: 使用 IVAX-1 进行免疫引发可增强树突状细胞 (DC) 的成熟以及将骨髓细胞募集到注射部位,从而导致引流淋巴结 (DLN) 中出现更多数量的中性粒细胞、单核细胞和抗原呈递 DC,而与抗原清除动力学无关。这在 DLN 中诱导了 IFN-γ+ 细胞岛,表明克隆扩张。IVAX-1 产生了强大的抗原特异性功能性 (IFN-γ+) T 细胞反应,并在肺和脾中产生了显着更高数量的流感特异性记忆 T 细胞。IVAX-1 在免疫后长达 60 天提供持久保护和出色的肺部病毒清除能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过利用多种 TLR 途径的协同先天免疫激活,该组合可优化 T 细胞启动,而不依赖于抗原库效应。我们的研究结果确定了关键的早期先天免疫事件和细胞介质,这些事件和细胞介质可驱动强大的 CMI,并证明 TLR 激动剂组合具有引发持久 T 细胞免疫的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,像 IVAX-1 这样的 TLR4/9 组合佐剂可以通过促进强大的细胞介导的免疫来增强亚基 疫苗 对抗流感的功效,这对于长期保护和病毒清除至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在鼠 H5N1 流感模型中进行的,这可能会限制对人类的直接推广。然而,多种先进技术的使用和多次检测的一致结果为研究结果提供了高度可信度。

papers.title: Contribution of Influenza H5 Head and Stalk Domains to the Development of Functional Non-Neutralizing Antibodies Following Mucosal rH5-NE Vaccination 2333118
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction In a prior Phase 1 trial we showed that an intranasal (IN) recombinant hemagglutinin (HA) H5 vaccine (rH5; A/Indo/05) nanoemulsion-adjuvanted (rH5 NE) and given on days 1 and 29 effectively primed the immune system. Participants received rH5 NE (25—100 μg; IN; n = 24), unadjuvanted rH5 (100 μg; IN; n = 7), or placebo (n = 6). Only rH5 NE recipients exhibited significant increases in HAI titers after a heterologous intramuscular (IM) H5N1 booster on day 197, confirming successful mucosal priming. Anti-H5 antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity also demonstrated this priming effect. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the contribution of influenza H5 head and stalk domains to functional non-neutralizing antibodies following mucosal rH5-NE vaccination. In a Phase 1 trial, participants received intranasal rH5 NE (25–100 μg; n=24), unadjuvanted rH5 (100 μg; n=7), or placebo (n=6). The vaccine induced cross-reactive ADCC and ADCP responses, primarily driven by antibodies targeting the H5-head domain. By day 57, 33% of rH5 NE recipients showed ADCC seroconversion, increasing to 50% after an intramuscular boost. Head-specific responses reached 88% by day 225, while stalk-specific responses were largely preexisting. The findings support the vaccine's capacity for effective mucosal priming against diverse H5 viruses.

papers.title: Local immune networks promote respiratory IgA responses after mucosal vaccination 2260370
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Mucosal immunization and respiratory IgA offer significant promise in protecting against airborne pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2. However, the conditions and mechanisms that lead to the robust induction of respiratory IgA responses following mucosal vaccination remain poorly understood. Methods In this project, we established SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection and mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination models. Using genetic mouse models and various in vivo and in vitro blockade or depletion approaches, we further investigated the mechanisms regulating respiratory IgA responses. Results Here we found that a mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination in mouse models revealed that respiratory booster immunization elicited markedly stronger and more durable respiratory IgA, T cell response, and protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2, supporting the promise of respiratory mucosal vaccination. papers.title: Evaluating AlphaFold 3 immune complex structure prediction and cryo-EM analysis of broadly neutralizing antibodies towards influenza hemagglutinin 2309571
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Epitope:paratope interactions define the breadth and affinity an antibody has towards an antigen. Computational structure prediction can help to model immune complexes as a method of in silico screening for broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). However, we do not currently understand how structural predictions and confidence metrics correlate with experimental data. Here, we evaluate the accuracy of AlphaFold 3 (AF3) in predicting immune complexes of a known class of bnAbs towards a conserved epitope on influenza hemagglutinin (HA). Methods We used single-cell RNA sequencing to generate a library of HA reactive, paired antibody sequences. AF3 was used to computationally model antibody-HA interactions. Antibodies were expressed and characterized with BLI, ELISA, and microneutralization assays. Negative stain electron microscopy (nsEM) and single particle cryo-electron microscopy (SPA cryo-EM) were used to structurally characterize immune complexes. Results B cell receptor sequencing of PBMCs from 23 healthy, human donors generated 1161 H5 HA-specific, paired antibody sequences. These sequences comprised new examples within a known class of antibodies (VH1-69, of which previous examples are in the AF3 training set) likely to target the conserved central stem. We modeled these antibody sequences in complex with H1N1 and H5N1 HAs using AF3. Highly confident predictions correlated with antibodies possessing high affinity and breadth. Moreover, in silico epitope footprints strongly matched experimental nsEM data. Finally, we resolved atomistic details with high-resolution SPA cryo-EM that explain challenges with AF3 immune complex prediction. Conclusion AF3 can be used to screen for VH1-69 bnAbs targeting a conserved epitope on influenza HA with high confidence. This method of down selection may be applied to other classes of antibodies and to other epitopes. However, models still need to be tuned to accurately predict immune complexes of novel or less characterized antibody classes. Funding Source Endowed Fellowship in the Skaggs Graduate School of Chemical and Biological Sciences, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). Topic Categories Computational and Systems Immunology (COMP)

papers.title_zh: 评估流感血凝素广泛中和抗体的 AlphaFold 3 免疫复合物结构预测和冷冻电镜分析 2309571
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Epitope:paratope interactions define the breadth and affinity an antibody has towards an antigen. Computational structure prediction can help to model immune complexes as a method of in silico screening for broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). However, we do not currently understand how structural predictions and confidence metrics correlate with experimental data. Here, we evaluate the accuracy of AlphaFold 3 (AF3) in predicting immune complexes of a known class of bnAbs towards a conserved epitope on influenza hemagglutinin (HA). Methods We used single-cell RNA sequencing to generate a library of HA reactive, paired antibody sequences. AF3 was used to computationally model antibody-HA interactions. Antibodies were expressed and characterized with BLI, ELISA, and microneutralization assays. Negative stain electron microscopy (nsEM) and single particle cryo-electron microscopy (SPA cryo-EM) were used to structurally characterize immune complexes. Results B cell receptor sequencing of PBMCs from 23 healthy, human donors generated 1161 H5 HA-specific, paired antibody sequences. These sequences comprised new examples within a known class of antibodies (VH1-69, of which previous examples are in the AF3 training set) likely to target the conserved central stem. We modeled these antibody sequences in complex with H1N1 and H5N1 HAs using AF3. Highly confident predictions correlated with antibodies possessing high affinity and breadth. Moreover, in silico epitope footprints strongly matched experimental nsEM data. Finally, we resolved atomistic details with high-resolution SPA cryo-EM that explain challenges with AF3 immune complex prediction. Conclusion AF3 can be used to screen for VH1-69 bnAbs targeting a conserved epitope on influenza HA with high confidence. This method of down selection may be applied to other classes of antibodies and to other epitopes. However, models still need to be tuned to accurately predict immune complexes of novel or less characterized antibody classes. Funding Source Endowed Fellowship in the Skaggs Graduate School of Chemical and Biological Sciences, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). Topic Categories Computational and Systems Immunology (COMP)
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 表位:互补位相互作用定义了抗体对抗原的广度和亲和力。计算结构预测有助于对免疫复合物进行建模,作为计算机筛选广泛中和抗体 (bnAb) 的方法。然而,我们目前还不了解结构预测和置信度指标如何与实验数据相关联。在这里,我们评估了 AlphaFold 3 (AF3) 在预测已知类别 bnAb 对流感血凝素 (HA) 保守表位的免疫复合物方面的准确性。方法 我们使用单细胞 RNA 测序来生成 HA 反应性配对抗体序列文库。AF3 用于计算模拟抗体-HA 相互作用。通过 BLI、ELISA 和微量中和测定来表达和表征抗体。使用负染色电子显微镜 (nsEM) 和单粒子冷冻电子显微镜 (SPA Cryo-EM) 对免疫复合物进行结构表征。结果 对 23 名健康人类捐赠者的 PBMC 进行 B 细胞受体测序,生成了 1161 个 H5 HA 特异性配对抗体序列。这些序列包含已知类别抗体(VH1-69,其中先前的示例位于 AF3 训练集中)中的新示例,可能以保守的中央茎为目标。我们使用 AF3 对这些抗体序列与 H1N1 和 H5N1 HA 的复合物进行建模。高度可信的预测与具有高亲和力和广度的抗体相关。此外,计算机表位足迹与实验 nsEM 数据高度匹配。最后,我们使用高分辨率 SPA 冷冻电镜解决了原子细节,解释了 AF3 免疫复合物预测的挑战。结论 AF3 可用于筛选针对流感 HA 保守表位的 VH1-69 bnAb,且可信度较高。这种向下选择的方法可以应用于其他类别的抗体和其他表位。然而,仍然需要调整模型以准确预测新型或特征较少的抗体类别的免疫复合物。资金来源:国家过敏和传染病研究所 (NIAID) 斯卡格斯化学与生物科学研究生院的奖学金。主题类别 计算和系统免疫学 (COMP)

news.content_title: Bird flu (avian influenza): latest situation in England
news.content: Bird flu (avian influenza): latest situation in England Find out about the latest bird flu situation in England and guidance for bird keepers and the public. Contents: - Latest situation - All bird flu cases and disease zones - Bird flu guidance - Bird gatherings - Vaccines - Latest GOV.UK news stories - Risk levels and outbreak assessments - Wild birds - Mammals - Bird flu webinars - Defra policies and contingency plans - Bird flu legislation Take action to prevent bird flu and stop it spreading. Be vigilant for signs of disease and report it to keep your birds safe. Latest situation The UK has self-declared freedom from highly pathogenic avian influenza (bird flu) for Great Britain on 18 May 2026. The avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) for poultry and captive birds in England, Wales and Scotland was lifted on 4 June 2026. All bird flu cases and disease control zones The first case of HPAI H5N1 of the 2025 to 2026 outbreak season was confirmed in: - England on 11 October 2025 - Scotland on 12 November 2025 - Wales on 25 October 2025 - Northern Ireland on 9 October 2025 Find details of all bird flu cases and disease zones in England. 2025 to 2026: summary of confirmed cases in the UK Previous outbreak seasons: summary of confirmed cases in the UK The season is recorded from 1 October to 30 September each year. Find details of previous bird flu cases and disease zones in England. Find details of previous bird flu cases in Scotland, cases in Wales and cases in Northern Ireland. Find details and assessments of past outbreaks in Great Britain in the Animal and Plant Health Agency’s outbreak epidemiology reports. Bird flu guidance Find out how to: - spot and report bird flu in poultry and other captive birds - report dead wild birds - prevent bird flu and stop it spreading - follow the rules in disease zones - check if you need a movement licence and how to apply - house your birds safely - follow the rules if you keep racing pigeons, birds of prey and other captive birds - hold a bird gathering You can read guidance about: - how to keep other pets safe from bird flu, such as cats and dogs - how bird flu spreads in wild birds and wild mammals, and how the government monitors it - avian influenza (bird flu) vaccination Bird gatherings If you are not in a disease control zone (such as a protection zone or surveillance zone) in England, follow the conditions in the general licences for gatherings of poultry and other captive birds. Read guidance on holding bird gatherings in England. Vaccines You cannot vaccinate poultry or most captive birds against bird flu in England. You can only vaccinate zoo birds in England if you meet eligibility criteria and get authorisation from APHA. Only zoos or collections holding a current zoo licence can apply for vaccination. Defra continues to invest in bird flu research and monitors the situation globally. We work with the Veterinary Medicines Directorate (VMD) to monitor the development of vaccines for birds. Find out more information on avian influenza (bird flu) vaccination and the work of the avian influenza vaccination taskforce. Latest GOV.UK news stories Risk levels and outbreak assessments The risk of HPAI H5 in wild birds in Great Britain is assessed as low (event occurs rarely). The risk of poultry exposure to HPAI H5 in Great Britain is assessed as: - low (event occurs rarely) (with low uncertainty) where there is suboptimal or poor biosecurity - low (event occurs rarely) (with low uncertainty) where stringent biosecurity is consistently applied at all times Find details of the evidence that supported these decisions in the: - risk and outbreak assessments - outbreak epidemiology reports - weekly reports of findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - findings of bird flu in non-avian wildlife - findings of bird flu in captive mammals The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) advise that bird flu is primarily a disease of birds and the risk to the general public’s health is very low. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has said bird flu poses a very low food safety risk for UK consumers. Properly cooked poultry and poultry products, including eggs, are safe to eat. Wild birds Find out how to report dead wild birds. Defra has set out practical information to support land managers, the public and ornithological and environmental organisations in their response to the growing threat of bird flu. The mitigation strategy for avian influenza in wild birds in England and Wales explains how these groups, together with the government and its delivery partners, can reduce the impact on wild bird populations whilst protecting public health, the wider environment and the rural economy. Landowners, local authorities and other organisations can download and print bird flu posters to display on site when there is a risk of bird flu or if bird flu has been detected in the area. Check the: - interactive map of reported wild bird mortality and findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - interactive dashboard of findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - weekly reports of HPAI findings in wild birds in Great Britain You can find out more about: - the collection thresholds for dead wild birds with suspected bird flu - how bird flu spreads in wild birds and wild mammals, and how the government monitors it Feeding wild birds You can feed wild birds but always wash your hands with soap and water afterwards. Avoid areas that have premises where poultry or captive birds are kept. Wild birds can spread bird flu to captive birds. If you’re in an avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) you cannot feed wild gamebirds within 500m of a premises with more than 500 poultry or captive birds. Check if you’re in a zone on the bird flu zone map and find out more in the guidance on rules if you keep game birds. If you feed wild birds in your garden, read advice from the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO) to keep feeders and water baths clean. This will help to stop bird flu and other diseases spreading between different birds. The UK Health Security Agency has said that the risk to the public from this bird flu strain is very low. It mainly affects birds. Do not touch or move any dead or sick wild birds – find out how to report them. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water if you touch wild bird faeces or feathers. For more advice go to the NHS website. Mammals Avian influenza (bird flu) viruses can also infect wild and kept mammals. This is known as influenza of avian origin. Find out how we monitor the risk of influenza of avian origin in wild mammals. Check the: - report of findings of influenza of avian origin in non-avian wildlife - interactive map showing findings of influenza of avian origin in wild mammals in Great Britain - findings of influenza of avian origin in captive mammals Influenza of avian origin in mammals is notifiable in both wild and kept mammals. You must report it immediately if you examine or inspect any wild or kept mammal, or analyse samples from any wild or kept mammal or mammal carcase and: - suspect the presence of influenza of avian origin - detect evidence of influenza A virus or antibodies to influenza A virus Report it immediately by calling: - 03000 200 301 if you’re in England - 03003 038 268 if you’re in Wales - your local Field Services Office if you’re in Scotland If you do not report it, you’re breaking the law. Bird flu webinars Whether you have pet birds, commercial flocks or just a few birds in a backyard flock, the avian influenza ‘stop the spread’ webinars explain what you can do to protect your birds. Defra policies and contingency plans Defra controls cases of bird flu by following the: - contingency plan for exotic notifiable diseases - notifiable avian disease control strategy - mitigation strategy for avian influenza in wild birds in England and Wales Bird flu legislation The legislation in England includes: - The Avian Influenza and Influenza of Avian Origin in Mammals (England) (No.2) Order 2006 - The Avian Influenza and Influenza of Avian Origin in Mammals (Amendment) (England) Order 2022 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) (EU Exit) Regulations 2018 - The Exotic Animal Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2021 - The Exotic Animal Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2022 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2023 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2024 - The Avian Influenza (H5N1 in Wild Birds) (England) Order 2006 - The Avian Influenza (H5N1 in Wild Birds) (England) (Amendment) Order 2021 - The Avian Influenza (Preventive Measures) (England) Regulations 2006 - The Transport of Animals (Cleansing and Disinfection) (England) (No. 3) Order 2003 - The Diseases of Animals (Approved Disinfectants) (England) Order 2007 - The Avian Influenza (Vaccination) (England) Regulations 2006 For Scotland go to the Scottish Government website. For Wales go to the Welsh Government website. For Northern Ireland go to the DAERA-NI website. Image on this page shows a group of ducks flying. Credit: Jari Hytönen. Updates to this page - The UK has self-declared freedom from highly pathogenic avian influenza (bird flu) for Great Britain on 18 May 2026. - Updated the guidance for bird gatherings - if you are not in a disease control zone (such as a protection zone or surveillance zone) in England, follow the conditions in the general licences for gatherings of poultry and other captive birds. - Updated to reflect that the avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) for poultry and captive birds in England, Wales and Scotland has been lifted. - Updated the risk levels for HPAI H5 in Great Britain in wild birds and poultry. - Following successful completion of disease control activities and surveillance in the zone around a fourth and fifth premises near Gainsborough, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire (AIV 2026/17 and AIV 2026/19). The 10km surveillance zone around each premises has been revoked. - Following successful completion of disease control activities and surveillance in the zone around a second premises near Great Shelford, South Cambridgeshire, Cambridgeshire (AIV 2026/18) the 3km protection zone has ended and the 10km surveillance zone has been revoked. - Following successful completion of disease control activities and surveillance in the zone around a second premises near Market Rasen, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire (AIV 2026/16) the surveillance zone has been revoked. - Following successful completion of disease control activities and surveillance in the zone around a second premises near Market Rasen, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire (AIV 2026/16) the 3km protection zone has ended and the area that formed it becomes part of the surveillance zone. - Corrected an error in the 17 April 2026 update to reflect that this is the fifth premises near Gainsborough, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire where Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 has been confirmed and not the fourth. - Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 was confirmed in a fourth large commercial poultry unit near Gainsborough, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire. A 3km protection zone and 10km surveillance zone has been declared around the premises. - Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 was confirmed in commercial poultry at a third premises near Gainsborough, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire, and near Great Shelford, South Cambridgeshire, Cambridgeshire. A 3km protection zone and 10km surveillance zone has been declared around each of the the premises. news.content_original: Bird flu (avian influenza): latest situation in England Find out about the latest bird flu situation in England and guidance for bird keepers and the public. Contents: - Latest situation - All bird flu cases and disease zones - Bird flu guidance - Bird gatherings - Vaccines - Latest GOV.UK news stories - Risk levels and outbreak assessments - Wild birds - Mammals - Bird flu webinars - Defra policies and contingency plans - Bird flu legislation Take action to prevent bird flu and stop it spreading. Be vigilant for signs of disease and report it to keep your birds safe. Latest situation The UK has self-declared freedom from highly pathogenic avian influenza (bird flu) for Great Britain on 18 May 2026. The avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) for poultry and captive birds in England, Wales and Scotland was lifted on 4 June 2026. All bird flu cases and disease control zones The first case of HPAI H5N1 of the 2025 to 2026 outbreak season was confirmed in: - England on 11 October 2025 - Scotland on 12 November 2025 - Wales on 25 October 2025 - Northern Ireland on 9 October 2025 Find details of all bird flu cases and disease zones in England. 2025 to 2026: summary of confirmed cases in the UK Previous outbreak seasons: summary of confirmed cases in the UK The season is recorded from 1 October to 30 September each year. Find details of previous bird flu cases and disease zones in England. Find details of previous bird flu cases in Scotland, cases in Wales and cases in Northern Ireland. Find details and assessments of past outbreaks in Great Britain in the Animal and Plant Health Agency’s outbreak epidemiology reports. Bird flu guidance Find out how to: - spot and report bird flu in poultry and other captive birds - report dead wild birds - prevent bird flu and stop it spreading - follow the rules in disease zones - check if you need a movement licence and how to apply - house your birds safely - follow the rules if you keep racing pigeons, birds of prey and other captive birds - hold a bird gathering You can read guidance about: - how to keep other pets safe from bird flu, such as cats and dogs - how bird flu spreads in wild birds and wild mammals, and how the government monitors it - avian influenza (bird flu) vaccination Bird gatherings If you are not in a disease control zone (such as a protection zone or surveillance zone) in England, follow the conditions in the general licences for gatherings of poultry and other captive birds. Read guidance on holding bird gatherings in England. Vaccines You cannot vaccinate poultry or most captive birds against bird flu in England. You can only vaccinate zoo birds in England if you meet eligibility criteria and get authorisation from APHA. Only zoos or collections holding a current zoo licence can apply for vaccination. Defra continues to invest in bird flu research and monitors the situation globally. We work with the Veterinary Medicines Directorate (VMD) to monitor the development of vaccines for birds. Find out more information on avian influenza (bird flu) vaccination and the work of the avian influenza vaccination taskforce. Latest GOV.UK news stories Risk levels and outbreak assessments The risk of HPAI H5 in wild birds in Great Britain is assessed as low (event occurs rarely). The risk of poultry exposure to HPAI H5 in Great Britain is assessed as: - low (event occurs rarely) (with low uncertainty) where there is suboptimal or poor biosecurity - low (event occurs rarely) (with low uncertainty) where stringent biosecurity is consistently applied at all times Find details of the evidence that supported these decisions in the: - risk and outbreak assessments - outbreak epidemiology reports - weekly reports of findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - findings of bird flu in non-avian wildlife - findings of bird flu in captive mammals The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) advise that bird flu is primarily a disease of birds and the risk to the general public’s health is very low. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has said bird flu poses a very low food safety risk for UK consumers. Properly cooked poultry and poultry products, including eggs, are safe to eat. Wild birds Find out how to report dead wild birds. Defra has set out practical information to support land managers, the public and ornithological and environmental organisations in their response to the growing threat of bird flu. The mitigation strategy for avian influenza in wild birds in England and Wales explains how these groups, together with the government and its delivery partners, can reduce the impact on wild bird populations whilst protecting public health, the wider environment and the rural economy. Landowners, local authorities and other organisations can download and print bird flu posters to display on site when there is a risk of bird flu or if bird flu has been detected in the area. Check the: - interactive map of reported wild bird mortality and findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - interactive dashboard of findings of bird flu in wild birds in Great Britain - weekly reports of HPAI findings in wild birds in Great Britain You can find out more about: - the collection thresholds for dead wild birds with suspected bird flu - how bird flu spreads in wild birds and wild mammals, and how the government monitors it Feeding wild birds You can feed wild birds but always wash your hands with soap and water afterwards. Avoid areas that have premises where poultry or captive birds are kept. Wild birds can spread bird flu to captive birds. If you’re in an avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) you cannot feed wild gamebirds within 500m of a premises with more than 500 poultry or captive birds. Check if you’re in a zone on the bird flu zone map and find out more in the guidance on rules if you keep game birds. If you feed wild birds in your garden, read advice from the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO) to keep feeders and water baths clean. This will help to stop bird flu and other diseases spreading between different birds. The UK Health Security Agency has said that the risk to the public from this bird flu strain is very low. It mainly affects birds. Do not touch or move any dead or sick wild birds – find out how to report them. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water if you touch wild bird faeces or feathers. For more advice go to the NHS website. Mammals Avian influenza (bird flu) viruses can also infect wild and kept mammals. This is known as influenza of avian origin. Find out how we monitor the risk of influenza of avian origin in wild mammals. Check the: - report of findings of influenza of avian origin in non-avian wildlife - interactive map showing findings of influenza of avian origin in wild mammals in Great Britain - findings of influenza of avian origin in captive mammals Influenza of avian origin in mammals is notifiable in both wild and kept mammals. You must report it immediately if you examine or inspect any wild or kept mammal, or analyse samples from any wild or kept mammal or mammal carcase and: - suspect the presence of influenza of avian origin - detect evidence of influenza A virus or antibodies to influenza A virus Report it immediately by calling: - 03000 200 301 if you’re in England - 03003 038 268 if you’re in Wales - your local Field Services Office if you’re in Scotland If you do not report it, you’re breaking the law. Bird flu webinars Whether you have pet birds, commercial flocks or just a few birds in a backyard flock, the avian influenza ‘stop the spread’ webinars explain what you can do to protect your birds. Defra policies and contingency plans Defra controls cases of bird flu by following the: - contingency plan for exotic notifiable diseases - notifiable avian disease control strategy - mitigation strategy for avian influenza in wild birds in England and Wales Bird flu legislation The legislation in England includes: - The Avian Influenza and Influenza of Avian Origin in Mammals (England) (No.2) Order 2006 - The Avian Influenza and Influenza of Avian Origin in Mammals (Amendment) (England) Order 2022 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) (EU Exit) Regulations 2018 - The Exotic Animal Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2021 - The Exotic Animal Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2022 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2023 - The Exotic Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2024 - The Avian Influenza (H5N1 in Wild Birds) (England) Order 2006 - The Avian Influenza (H5N1 in Wild Birds) (England) (Amendment) Order 2021 - The Avian Influenza (Preventive Measures) (England) Regulations 2006 - The Transport of Animals (Cleansing and Disinfection) (England) (No. 3) Order 2003 - The Diseases of Animals (Approved Disinfectants) (England) Order 2007 - The Avian Influenza (Vaccination) (England) Regulations 2006 For Scotland go to the Scottish Government website. For Wales go to the Welsh Government website. For Northern Ireland go to the DAERA-NI website. Image on this page shows a group of ducks flying. Credit: Jari Hytönen. analysis.location_and_population: England, with references to Great Britain, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. The affected population includes poultry, captive birds, wild birds, and mammals.
analysis.event: The UK government has declared freedom from HPAI H5N1 for Great Britain and lifted the AIPZ. The first case of HPAI H5N1 in the 2025-2026 outbreak season was confirmed in England on 11 October 2025. The risk to the general public's health is assessed as very low.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Confirmed cases of HPAI H5N1 were reported in England (11 October 2025), Scotland (12 November 2025), Wales (25 October 2025), and Northern Ireland (9 October 2025). The risk of HPAI H5 in wild birds and poultry exposure is assessed as low (event occurs rarely). The risk to the general public's health is very low, and the food safety risk for UK consumers is also very low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The AIPZ was lifted on 4 June 2026. The government continues to monitor the situation globally and invest in bird flu research. Vaccination is restricted to zoo birds with authorization. The UK Health Security Agency and Food Standards Agency advise that properly cooked poultry and poultry products are safe to eat. Public guidance includes reporting dead wild birds and maintaining biosecurity.

The risk to the general public's health is assessed as very low, and properly cooked poultry products remain safe. The government continues to monitor the situation globally, restrict vaccination to authorized zoo birds, and provide guidance on biosecurity and reporting dead wild birds.

elements_zh.location_and_population: 英格兰,指的是大不列颠、苏格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰。受影响的种群包括家禽、圈养鸟类、野生鸟类 和哺乳动物。
elements_zh.event: 英国政府已宣布英国免受 HPAI H5N1 感染,并解除了 AIPZ。2025 年 10 月 11 日,英格兰确认了 2025-2026 暴发 季节的首例 HPAI H5N1 病例。评估对公众健康的风险非常低。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 英格兰(2025年10月11日)、苏格兰(2025年11月12日)、威尔士(2025年10月25日)和北爱尔兰(2025年10月9日)报告了HPAI H5N1确诊病例。野生鸟类 和家禽暴露中 HPAI H5 的风险评估为低(事件很少发生)。对公众健康的风险非常低,英国消费者的食品安全风险也非常低。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: AIPZ 于 2026 年 6 月 4 日解除。政府继续监测全球局势并投资禽流感研究。疫苗接种仅限于经授权的动物园鸟类。英国健康安全局和食品标准局建议,正确煮熟的家禽和家禽产品可以安全食用。公共指导包括报告死亡 野生鸟类 和维护生物安全。

Vaccination is restricted to zoo birds with authorization. The UK Health Security Agency and Food Standards Agency advise that properly cooked poultry and poultry products are safe to eat. Public guidance includes reporting dead wild birds and maintaining biosecurity.

news.source_body_en: The UK government has declared freedom from highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) for Great Britain, with the avian influenza prevention zone (AIPZ) lifted on 4 June 2026. The first case of HPAI H5N1 in the 2025-2026 season was confirmed in England on 11 October 2025, with additional cases reported in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. The risk to the general public's health is assessed as very low, and properly cooked poultry products remain safe. The government continues to monitor the situation globally, restrict vaccination to authorized zoo birds, and provide guidance on biosecurity and reporting dead wild birds.

analysis.brief_en: The New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries has confirmed the detection of bird flu (HPAI) in individual wild birds within the country. In response, authorities have established a hotline and online reporting system for citizens to report groups of three or more sick or dead wild birds. The government is providing guidance to the public on how to limit the impact of the virus and be prepared for potential further spread. While the detection is confirmed in individual birds, no specific case numbers, deaths, or broader risk assessments have been disclosed. The focus remains on surveillance, reporting mechanisms, and public education to protect native species.

While the detection is confirmed in individual birds, no specific case numbers, deaths, or broader risk assessments have been disclosed. The focus remains on surveillance, reporting mechanisms, and public education to protect native species.

news.content_zh: 新西兰第一产业部已确认在该国境内个体 野生鸟类 中检测到禽流感 (HPAI)。为此,当局建立了热线电话和在线报告系统,供公民报告三人或三人以上患病或死亡的群体 野生鸟类。政府正在向公众提供有关如何限制病毒影响并为潜在的进一步传播做好准备的指导。虽然在个别鸟类中证实了这一检测,但尚未披露具体的病例数、死亡人数或更广泛的风险评估。重点仍然是 监测、报告机制和保护本土物种的公共教育。

news.content_title: Wild bird surveillance reveals how H5Nx flu keeps returning to China
news.content: Two decades of monitoring show how migratory birds, viral reassortment, and global flyways are reshaping the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza. Study: Evolving dynamics of H5Nx avian influenza in China revealed by long-term wild bird surveillance . Image Credit: GatisVil / Shutterstock In a recent study published as an Article in Press in the journal Nature Communications , a group of researchers investigated the long-term evolution, transmission, and geographic spread of H5Nx highly pathogenic avian influenza virus ( HPAIV ) in China's wild birds through nationwide surveillance and genomic analyses. Background Avian flu outbreaks affect millions of birds, disrupting global poultry production and threatening wildlife conservation and public health. Highly pathogenic avian influenza ( HPAI ) H5Nx viruses have far exceeded their original geographic range by spreading across continents with the help of migratory birds and often engaging in the exchange of genetic material. Since various continents are connected through migratory flyways, it is important to determine the pattern of the spread of these viruses and the manner in which they evolve. Further research is needed to strengthen international surveillance and improve early detection of newly emerging viral lineages. About the study The researchers conducted nationwide surveillance of avian influenza viruses ( AIVs ) in wild birds across China from February 2003 through February 2023. During this period, 219,445 samples were collected from 28 provincial-level regions. Surveillance before 2013 was largely restricted to northeastern China, especially Heilongjiang Province, but this changed after the establishment of the Bird Flu Monitoring and Alert System ( BFMAS ) in 2014. The surveillance project included both active monitoring with live birds and passive surveillance with reports of sick and dead birds. Samples collected included fresh fecal samples, tissues, and swabs from various sources. The specimens collected were transported under temperature-controlled conditions and underwent virus isolation in specific pathogen-free embryonic chicken eggs. Identification of the viruses was done through hemagglutination tests, subtyping, ribonucleic acid ( RNA ) extraction, amplification, and Sanger sequencing. The scientists performed a thorough analysis of global outbreak cases from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) records, as well as obtained open-source genome sequence data from the Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data ( GISAID ) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information ( NCBI ) databases. Phylogenetic, phylogeographic, statistical, and evolutionary analyses were then performed to evaluate viral diversity, transmission pathways, geographic spread, host transitions, and long-term evolutionary patterns of H5Nx viruses. Study results Nationwide surveillance identified substantial changes in the occurrence and distribution of H5Nx HPAIVs over the 20-year monitoring period. Researchers collected 219,445 bird samples in China from February 2003 to February 2023 and isolated 1,344 AIVs , yielding an overall isolation rate of 0.61%. Prior to 2014, there was limited monitoring, and no H5Nx HPAIVs were detected . Following the introduction of the BFMAS , surveillance expanded considerably, yielding 368 H5Nx HPAIV isolates, including H5N1, H5N2, H5N6, and H5N8 viruses. Viral activity showed a clear seasonal pattern, with peaks between November and January and a drop-off in summer. Interestingly, no H5Nx HPAIVs were detected between mid-2017 and late 2020, despite the continued circulation of low-pathogenic avian influenza viruses ( LPAIVs ), suggesting possible suppression rather than confirming the absence of transmission. Temporal shifts in viral subtypes were also evident. H5N1 predominated during 2014-2015, H5N8 became the dominant subtype during 2016-2017 and 2020, and H5N1 re-emerged between 2021 and 2023. These transitions closely mirrored global changes in clade 2.3.4.4b viruses and reflected ongoing viral evolution through antigenic drift, reassortment, and host immune pressures. The surveillance program documented 46 distinct H5Nx HPAIV detection events, revealing marked geographic and seasonal variation. Most detections occurred along major migratory flyways, particularly the Central Asia Flyway and the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, with approximately three-quarters of events recorded between September and February during migration and overwintering seasons. Phylogenetic analyses identified three major viral clades circulating in China, with clade 2.3.4.4b as the dominant lineage, exhibiting the greatest genetic diversity and geographic distribution. This clade continued to evolve through reassortment, creating multiple H5N1 and H5N8 genotypes over time. Worldwide outbreak analyses also showed that, while poultry accounted for the majority of outbreaks throughout the study period, outbreaks linked to wild birds grew significantly after 2016 and often outnumbered poultry outbreaks from autumn 2020 onward. Phylogeographic analysis revealed that the majority of earlier H5Nx transmission events occurred in East Asia, whereas more recent viruses found in China were genetically closer to viruses circulating in Europe and North Asia than to locally derived variants. Most clade 2.3.4.4b viruses detected after 2020 were consistent with repeated reintroductions through migratory birds rather than continuous local transmission. Conclusion The findings showed that long-term surveillance of wild birds contributes to a better understanding of the evolution, reassortment, and worldwide spread of H5Nx HPAIVs . According to the research, clade 2.3.4.4b has emerged as the dominant lineage mediating intercontinental spread, and the latest viruses found in China largely represent repeated reintroductions through migratory birds rather than sustained local circulation. These observations emphasize the need for ongoing surveillance, genomic monitoring, and international cooperation to detect new viral variants and explore their routes of transmission. Journal reference: Li, X., Lv, X., Li, Y., Fei, M., Zhang, S., An, Q., Qin, S., Peng, P., Li, J., Liang, H., Xiu, Y., Li, Z., Wang, Y., Wang, Y., Zeng, X., Hou, Z., Sun, H., Xu, Y., Li, Y., & Chai, H. (2026). Evolving dynamics of H5Nx avian influenza in China revealed by long-term wild bird surveillance. Nature Communications . DOI : 10.1038/s41467-026-76039-9, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-76039-9

analysis_en.location_and_population: The surveillance was conducted nationwide across China, covering 28 provincial-level regions. It focused on wild birds, including both active monitoring of live birds and passive surveillance of sick and dead birds, particularly along major migratory flyways like the Central Asia Flyway and the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.
analysis_en.event: A long-term study published in Nature Communications investigated the evolution, transmission, and geographic spread of H5Nx highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) in China's wild birds through nationwide surveillance and genomic analyses. The research confirmed that H5Nx HPAIVs were reintroduced to China through migratory birds rather than sustained local circulation.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Over 20 years, 219,445 samples were collected, yielding 1,344 avian influenza virus isolates (0.61% isolation rate). After 2014, 368 H5Nx HPAIV isolates were detected, including H5N1, H5N2, H5N6, and H5N8 subtypes. The study documented 46 distinct H5Nx HPAIV detection events, with most occurring during migration and overwintering seasons. Globally, outbreaks linked to wild birds grew significantly after 2016, often outnumbering poultry outbreaks from autumn 2020 onward.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The findings highlight the need for ongoing surveillance, genomic monitoring, and international cooperation to detect new viral variants. The study noted that while H5Nx HPAIVs were absent between mid-2017 and late 2020, low-pathogenic avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) continued to circulate, suggesting possible suppression rather than confirmed absence of transmission. The research emphasized the role of migratory birds in the intercontinental spread of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses.

news.source_body_en: A 20-year nationwide surveillance study in China, published in Nature Communications, reveals how H5Nx highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) are repeatedly reintroduced through migratory birds rather than sustained local circulation. Researchers collected 219,445 wild bird samples from 2003 to 2023, isolating 1,344 avian influenza viruses (0.61% rate). After expanding surveillance in 2014, 368 H5Nx HPAIVs were detected, including H5N1, H5N2, H5N6, and H5N8 subtypes. Viral activity peaked seasonally between November and January, with a notable absence of H5Nx HPAIVs from mid-2017 to late 2020. Phylogenetic analyses showed that most recent viruses in China were genetically closer to European and North Asian strains, indicating repeated reintroductions via migratory flyways. The study underscores the need for enhanced international surveillance and genomic monitoring to track viral evolution and spread.

news.content_title: First detection of deadly H5N1 bird flu confirmed in Victoria
news.content: Add us as a preferred source on Google Authorities in Victoria are increasing surveillance of wild animal populations after the detection of the state’s first case of the potentially catastrophic new strain of H5N1 bird flu. A member of the public discovered the ill bird in the coastal town of Portland near the border with South Australia and reported it to authorities. Testing on the greater crested tern subsequently confirmed the bird had contracted the virus. The detection comes after a series of cases in Western Australia , South Australia , New South Wales and Queensland . Victoria’s chief veterinary officer Graeme Cooke urged anyone who finds a cluster of at least five sick birds of any species to alert authorities. However, he said even a single sick or dead seabird, waterbird, shorebird or bird of prey – or marine mammal, such as seals and dolphins – should be reported to authorities immediately. “We recognise this can be unsettling news for members of our community,” Cooke said. The virus can devastate poultry and wildlife populations. The latest strain has authorities and farmers on edge amid concerns about an outbreak on poultry farms. The detection of a separate bird flu strain on farms in 2024 resulted in about 1.3 million birds being euthanised, followed by about 600,000 in 2025. Since the detection of the H5N1 virus in Western Australia last month, poultry keepers have been asked to voluntarily house their birds. In Victoria, that period has now been extended to a minimum of 14 days from today. H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been declared ineradicable by authorities, following confirmation on Wednesday that the virus is circulating among local birds. The national committee on emergency animal diseases, which comprises state and federal chief veterinary officers, as well as scientific experts, said now the virus had spread among local terns it was not feasible to stamp it out of the country. The official declaration triggers national co-ordination for cost sharing in response to the deadly virus. The Albanese government has already committed $113 million to preparations to deal with an H5N1 incursion, with an emphasis on planning to identify an outbreak swiftly and a response to limit its spread. This includes funding to prepare biosecurity officers to respond to an outbreak in farmed poultry, which may involve quarantining farms or districts and restricting transport between locations. Authorities are using aerial surveillance methods, with helicopters and drones monitoring wildlife populations. Victoria’s chief biodiversity officer James Todd said seal and gannet colonies in Portland were among the wildlife vulnerable to the disease. “We’ve been preparing for H5 arrival in Victoria for a few years now,” he said. Despite the technological response to the virus detection, Todd said co-operation from the community remained the most effective control method at hand. “Our best line of defence at this stage is still the Victorian public.” In a statement, Wildlife Victoria said it received a call from a concerned member of the public earlier this week about the greater crested tern in Portland showing signs of the virus. “Wildlife Victoria monitored the case until Agriculture Victoria responders arrived on scene to contain and test the bird,” it said. “The tern was confirmed positive to H5 bird flu shortly after.” Victorian Farmers Federation president Ryan Milgate said farmers should review their biosecurity plans and look out for unusual illness or unexplained bird deaths. “There has been no spread to commercial poultry flocks or any agricultural environment at this stage, and the risk to human health remains very low,” he said. The signs of H5N1 in birds include lack of co-ordination, tremors, swimming in circles, twisted necks, inability to fly or stand, diarrhoea, breathing difficulties, coughing, sneezing, swelling around the head, neck and eyes as well as cloudy eyes and changes in eye colour, as well as sudden death. analysis.event: Confirmed first detection of H5N1 bird flu in Victoria. A member of the public reported an ill bird, which was subsequently confirmed to have contracted the virus. The event is confirmed and involves authorities including Agriculture Victoria and Wildlife Victoria.

analysis.brief_en: Victoria has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain after a member of the public reported an ill greater crested tern in Portland. Testing confirmed the bird had contracted the virus, prompting authorities to increase surveillance of wild animal populations and urge poultry keepers to house their birds for at least 14 days. The H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been declared ineradicable, with the Australian government committing $113 million to response efforts. While the risk to human health is very low, authorities are concerned about potential impacts on poultry and wildlife, with previous outbreaks resulting in millions of birds being euthanized. Community cooperation is highlighted as crucial for controlling the spread.

news.content_title: Bird flu has reached Victoria and more wildlife deaths loom. How bad could it get?
news.content: Victoria confirmed its first case of the H5N1 bird flu virus on Thursday, in a greater crested tern in Portland. Photograph: DEA/P Jaccod/De Agostini/Getty Images Victoria confirmed its first case of the H5N1 bird flu virus on Thursday, in a greater crested tern in Portland. Photograph: DEA/P Jaccod/De Agostini/Getty Images Bird flu has reached Victoria and more wildlife deaths loom. How bad could it get? Authorities say local transmission of H5 bird flu virus among South Australian birds signals ‘shift in the situation’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia has entered a new phase in dealing with the incursion of deadly H5N1 bird flu , with authorities confirming on Wednesday that local transmission had taken place, and Victoria confirming first case of the highly virulent strain Thursday. “We have had what is suggestive of local transmission for the first time,” Julie Collins, the federal minister for agriculture, fisheries and forestry, said on Wednesday afternoon, after 11 suspected detections were reported in South Australian birds. “We will expect to see increased evidence and deaths of wildlife ... given there has been some local transmission,” she said. “This small shift in the situation will be very disappointing to many, but is certainly not an unexpected development as the last continent to detect H5 bird flu.” On Thursday morning, South Australia reported 13 more cases in greater crested terns. Now that authorities believe transmission of H5 strain is occurring locally, what does this mean for Australia’s wildlife, and how bad could things get? What’s the current status of H5N1 bird flu in Australia? On Thursday, South Australian authorities announced 13 new suspected bird flu detections in greater crested terns, including five cases at Seal Bay on Kangaroo Island, home to a population of endangered Australian sea lions. Victoria also detected its first case of the virus, in a greater crested tern in Portland. Once the new cases are confirmed, that would bring Australia to a total of 41 cases. Julie Collins, the agriculture minister, said the Consultative Committee on Emergency Animal Diseases – comprising federal and state and territory authorities – had met on Wednesday and agreed that “some local transmission has occurred between a number of greater crested terns that are resident in South Australia”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Dr Beth Cookson, Australia’s chief veterinary officer, said genetic sequencing showed all confirmed cases detected to date were related to subantarctic strains of the virus. Clare Scriven, the SA minister for primary industries, said earlier on Wednesday: “This is concerning but not unexpected. We knew that eventually when bird flu arrived in Australia it would spread. It has spread on every other continent around the globe.” What does the arrival of bird flu in Australia mean for poultry and will eggs be more expensive? Read more To date, there have been no H5 detections in poultry or agricultural industries in Australia. “The risk to human health remains low,” Collins said. How could bird flu affect wildlife on Kangaroo Island? Six of the Kangaroo Island bird flu detections have been at Seal Bay, home to the country’s third-largest Australian sea lion population. Conservationists have expressed fears for the sea lion population there. Alexia Wellbelove, campaigns director at the Australian Marine Conservation Society (AMCS), said Australian sea lions were “now on the frontline of the potential wildlife crisis”. About 80% of the Australian sea lion population is found in South Australia. The endangered mammal has seen populations decline by 60% in four decades , with remaining numbers about 12,000. “In South America, this virus killed 30,000 sea lion pups in just six months following transmission from birds to marine mammals,” Wellbelove said. “On our own Heard Island, it killed more than 13,000 elephant seal pups in a single season ... we now have to face the very real possibility of similar devastation here at home, in a species already teetering on the edge.” Scriven said on-beach tours at Seal Bay were temporarily paused to keep people separate from the “very vulnerable” animal population and to reduce the risk of spreading infection. What can be done to stop the spread of bird flu? Not much, unfortunately. Cookson said on Wednesday: “We do know from the overseas experience that once the virus becomes more widespread in wild bird populations it will not be possible to avoid losses in susceptible wildlife in the natural environment.” Authorities had anticipated the arrival of H5N1 in Australia through migratory birds “for a number of years”, she said. They will continue to focus on surveillance, to confirm where the virus is circulating and to “reduce the impacts where possible”. Collins said the federal government had invested more than $113m preparing for the virus’s arrival. “We have also, working with states and territories, now released a further $24m.” Without listing specific animals, Cookson said the government was taking “a number of actions in high-priority conservation species, including site- and species-specific planning”. There would also be a focus on protecting captive breeding populations, and implementing farm biosecurity measures to “limit contact between wild birds and poultry”. Groups including the AMCS and the Invasive Species Council have called on the federal government to establish a $200m national wildlife resilience fund, “focused on emergency protection and recovery for our most at-risk species”. How bad could bird flu get in Australia? Worldwide, the H5N1 variant has caused “unprecedented levels of ongoing outbreaks”, killing millions of wild birds and tens of thousands of mammals. A deadly strain of bird flu has landed on Australian shores. Does it pose a risk to pets? Read more Large-scale deaths have not yet occurred in Australia, but the major concerns relate to potential wildlife impacts: more than 150 native bird species have been assessed as being at “very high risk” of extinction or major decline if they are infected – including the red goshawk, fairy tern, plains-wanderer, shy albatross, black swan and western hooded plover. More than 10 mammal species are at very high risk, including the Australian sea lion, the subantarctic fur seal and the Australian fur seal. There could also be significant impacts on the poultry industry. Globally, an estimated 140m farmed birds have died or been culled since January last year. In the United States, the virus was linked to a 220% spike in egg prices in the first quarter of 2025. Western Australia’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry has warned that if the virus were to reach commercial flocks, it could push egg prices above $10 a carton. Mass culls could be necessary, and the RSPCA has called for fast-tracked research into more humane killing methods, such as the use of nitrogen in gas or foam. Human-to-human transmission of the virus is not common, but since 2003 there have been 1,000 reported cases of H5N1 in humans globally, with a 48% fatality rate .
